#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/lib/proc-group.sh — process-group resolution and kill helpers.
# Extracted from core/router/route.sh (Wave 15-G, #687) so the test stage and
# any other long-running spawn share one implementation (#1748).
# Sourced library: no set -euo pipefail.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_PROC_GROUP_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_PROC_GROUP_LOADED=1

# #2056: there is no setsid prefix any more. Process groups come from `set -m`
# at the spawn site — bash job control makes a backgrounded job a group leader,
# which is POSIX and identical on macOS and Linux.
#
# `setsid -w` was wrong here twice over. It is absent on macOS (util-linux is
# keg-only), so the prefix went empty, no group was created, and an abort
# degraded to a single-PID kill while every descendant survived — the Wave 15-G
# guarantee held on Linux only, and the test covering it is Linux-only too, so
# nothing said so. And `-w` forces setsid to fork, because it waits for the
# child and returns its exit status, so the pid the caller captured was the
# wrapper rather than the new session leader.
#
# Do not reintroduce a prefix here. A spawn that needs an external binary to get
# a process group is a spawn whose guarantee is platform-conditional.

# Prints the PGID safe to signal for <pid>, or nothing. Empty is not "no group":
# it means the group could not be proven distinct from ours, and signalling it
# would take down the runner itself — so callers must fall back to a PID kill.
zbuild_pg_resolve() {
    local _pid="${1:-}"
    [[ -n "$_pid" && "$_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
    local _child _self
    _child="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$_pid" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
    if [[ -n "$_child" && -n "$_self" && "$_child" != "$_self" ]]; then
        printf '%s' "$_child"
        return 0
    fi
    # A short-lived child can exit before `ps` reports it. Under `set -m` the
    # spawn IS the group leader, so PGID == PID by construction and that stays
    # true after it is gone — reporting the pid is correct, not a guess.
    #
    # This branch previously justified itself with "setsid execs in place, so it
    # needs no fork". That was false under `-w` (#2056): setsid forks in order to
    # wait, so the captured pid was the wrapper and the group belonged to a
    # process one fork below. Under job control there is no wrapper to be wrong
    # about.
    if [[ -z "$_child" ]]; then
        printf '%s' "$_pid"
    fi
}

# TERM <target>, then KILL whatever is left after <grace_s>. Shared by the group
# and single-PID paths so both get the same grace — the escalation is the whole
# contract, and a caller that skips it is indistinguishable from a plain KILL.
#
# Synchronous by construction (#905): the `{ sleep 1 && kill -KILL; } &` backstop
# this replaces could outlive the caller that armed it, so teardown returned
# while the tree was still alive and the backstop was sometimes lost with it.
# Polling instead costs milliseconds when the target exits on TERM, costs the
# full grace only when it ignores TERM, and leaves nothing running on return.
_zbuild_pg_term_then_kill() {
    # `--` because a group target is spelled `-PGID` and would otherwise parse
    # as an option.
    local _target="$1" _grace="$2"
    kill -TERM -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || true
    local _ticks=$(( _grace * 10 )) _i=0
    while (( _i < _ticks )); do
        kill -0 -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || return 0
        sleep 0.1 2>/dev/null || true
        _i=$(( _i + 1 ))
    done
    kill -KILL -- "$_target" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# A non-numeric grace would evaluate to 0 in the arithmetic context above, so the
# poll loop would never run and the target would go straight to KILL — silently
# losing the escalation the caller asked for. Clamp to the default instead.
_zbuild_pg_grace() {
    local _g="${1:-1}"
    [[ "$_g" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_g" -gt 0 ]] && printf '%s' "$_g" || printf '1'
}

# zbuild_pg_record_pgid <file> — the pgid out of a `.pgid` record.
#
# ONE reader, because there are two formats on disk and three places that read
# them (#2018). The engine's dispatch record is `<pgid>\t<leader start time>`;
# tool/test's own `test-stage.pgid` is a bare number; and a record written before
# #2018 is bare too. A reader that only understands one of those does not error —
# it fails the numeric guard and `continue`s, so the caller kills NOTHING and
# reports success. That is how a format change here silently disables ADR-062 §2
# reclamation, which is the path that actually runs on every normal exit.
#
# Prints nothing and returns 1 when there is no usable pgid, so a caller can
# still distinguish "no record" from "record says 1234".
zbuild_pg_record_pgid() {
    local _f="${1:-}" _pgid=""
    [[ -n "$_f" && -f "$_f" ]] || return 1
    IFS=$'\t' read -r _pgid _ 2>/dev/null < "$_f" || true
    [[ "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
    printf '%s' "$_pgid"
}

# zbuild_pg_register <pgid> — record a process group the caller just created.
#
# ADR-062 §1 had the ENGINE record this at dispatch. It could not, and the reason
# is structural: a stage is a bash function call, not a subprocess, so at the
# dispatch seam no group exists yet. That code fell back to `$$`'s group — the
# engine's own — which teardown then skipped, correctly, because signalling your
# own group takes the runner down with it. Every record was unkillable, every
# record was skipped, and §2's kill loop never freed anything (#2024).
#
# So the direction reverses: whoever CREATES a group registers it. Two sites do,
# and only two — `tool/test`'s `set -m` suite and the router's `setsid` spawn.
#
# Refusing to register our own group is the invariant, not a safety check. A
# record naming the registrar's own group is strictly worse than no record: it
# cannot be acted on, and it makes the mechanism look live while it does nothing
# — which is exactly how the original defect survived #2001, #2018 and an ADR.
#
# Fail-open throughout: a spawn is never refused because bookkeeping was
# unavailable. Silence here costs a possible leak; failing here costs the run.
zbuild_pg_register() {
    local _pgid="${1:-}"
    [[ -n "$_pgid" && "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
    local _self
    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
    [[ -n "$_self" && "$_self" == "$_pgid" ]] && return 0
    local _sd="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"
    [[ -n "$_sd" && -d "$_sd" ]] || return 0
    local _stage="${2:-${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}}"
    [[ -n "$_stage" ]] || return 0
    # One path component, sanitised the same way stage scratch keys are, so no
    # stage name can climb out of runtime/.
    _stage="${_stage//[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/_}"
    local _dir="${_sd}/runtime/stages"
    mkdir -p "$_dir" 2>/dev/null || return 0
    # #2018 format: the leader's start time proves the pgid still names what
    # recorded it, so a later sweep cannot signal a recycled pid.
    local _start
    _start="$(ps -o lstart= -p "$_pgid" 2>/dev/null | tr -s ' ' | sed 's/^ *//;s/ *$//' || true)"
    printf '%s\t%s' "$_pgid" "$_start" > "${_dir}/${_stage}.pgid" 2>/dev/null || true
    return 0
}

# TERM then KILL a whole process group. `-PGID` is the negative-pid convention.
zbuild_pg_kill() {
    local _pgid="${1:-}"
    [[ -n "$_pgid" && "$_pgid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
    # Refuse our own group: `kill -- -PGID` from inside it takes down the runner.
    local _self
    _self="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$$" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
    [[ -n "$_self" && "$_self" == "$_pgid" ]] && return 0
    _zbuild_pg_term_then_kill "-$_pgid" "$(_zbuild_pg_grace "${2:-}")"
}

# TERM then KILL a single PID — the path taken when no group could be proven.
# It gets the same grace as the group path: a suite that flushes coverage or
# writes partial results on SIGTERM needs the window wherever it is killed from.
zbuild_pid_kill() {
    local _pid="${1:-}"
    [[ -n "$_pid" && "$_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 0
    _zbuild_pg_term_then_kill "$_pid" "$(_zbuild_pg_grace "${2:-}")"
}

2	# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
3	# ║  plugin-registry — lifecycle hook dispatch + fail-closed output scanner    ║
4	# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
5	#
6	# Split from registry.sh (#364). Owns the runtime dispatch path:
7	# `plugin_hook_call` (sources plugin.sh in an isolated subshell, applies
8	# pre-source tamper checks, calls the hook function, then verifies declared
9	# outputs) and `scan_plugin_outputs` (ADR-001 fail-closed artifact-presence
10	# scanner). Depends on yaml_get / verify_plugin_for_source from the other two
11	# split modules — sourced together via the registry.sh facade.
12	# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail settings; do not add set -euo pipefail.
13	
14	[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_REGISTRY_LIFECYCLE_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
15	_ZBUILD_REGISTRY_LIFECYCLE_LOADED=1
16	
17	# #1809 (ADR-058 C9): declared-output path resolution is shared with
18	# core/pipeline/write-boundary.sh so the artifact scanner and the write-boundary
19	# classifier can never disagree about where a declared output lives.
20	# shellcheck source=output-paths.sh
21	source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/output-paths.sh"
22	# shellcheck source=write-ownership.sh
23	source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/write-ownership.sh"
24	# shellcheck source=attempt-archive.sh
25	source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/attempt-archive.sh"
26	# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/stage-dispatch-mark.sh
27	source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)/scripts/lib/stage-dispatch-mark.sh"
28	
29	# ─── scan_plugin_outputs — fail-closed artifact-presence scanner (#288) ─────
30	# ADR-001 §Fail-closed scanner contract:
31	#   "If a plugin declares an output but no artifact exists at outputs[].path
32	#    after run completes with exit 0, the engine emits a synthetic blocking
33	#    finding."
34	# #1906 retired provides.artifact_type, which the original wording keyed on;
35	# outputs[].required is the single declaration the scan now honours.
36	#
37	# Arguments:
38	#   $1 — plugin_dir
39	#   $2 — state_file (so $state_dir / $artifacts_dir can substitute into paths)
40	#
41	# Returns:
42	#   0 if all declared outputs are present (or no outputs declared).
43	#   1 if any declared output is missing — and emits one
44	#      `plugin.artifact.missing` event per missing path.
45	#
46	# Path-template substitution (Phase 0.5): supports ${state_dir} and
47	# ${artifact_dir} / ${artifacts_dir}. Any other ${VAR} resolves from the work
48	# unit's exported environment (#1803) — per-member outputs such as review-lens's
49	# `lens-${ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID}.json` (ADR-047 §2) are only checkable once the
50	# element var is expanded. A var that is unset stays literal and fails the check.
51	scan_plugin_outputs() {
52	    local plugin_dir="$1"
53	    local state_file="${2:-}"
54	    local stage="${3:-}"
55	    # #2252: `probe` answers present-or-not with no events, findings or marker.
56	    local probe="${4:-}"
57	    local manifest="$plugin_dir/manifest.yaml"
58	
59	    # No manifest, no outputs to scan — silently succeed.
60	    [[ ! -f "$manifest" ]] && return 0
61	
62	    local plugin_id; plugin_id="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "id" 2>/dev/null || true)"
63	    local kind; kind="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "kind" 2>/dev/null || true)"
64	    # ADR-047 §4 capability flag: build legitimately writes a zero-byte diff.patch
65	    # when a turn changed no code. The exemption is deliberately narrow — it never
66	    # covers a `primary: true` output, so a stage cannot mask an empty verdict
67	    # artifact (e.g. build-summary.json) by declaring the flag in its own manifest.
68	    local empty_diff_ok; empty_diff_ok="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "capabilities.empty_diff_legitimate" 2>/dev/null || true)"
69	
70	    # Compute substitution roots from state_file.
71	    local state_dir="" artifact_dir=""
72	    if [[ -n "$state_file" ]]; then
73	        state_dir="$(dirname "$state_file")"
74	        artifact_dir="${state_dir}/artifacts"
75	    fi
76	
77	    # Pull outputs[].path entries from the manifest. yaml_get/yaml_get_list
78	    # don't model lists of objects, so grep the YAML directly. Format we
79	    # support (per ADR-001):
80	    #   outputs:
81	    #     - name: foo
82	    #       path: ${artifact_dir}/foo.json
83	    #       type: foo.json
84	    # #511 F2: respect `required: false` on outputs. Without this, the scanner
85	    # would flag a legitimately optional artifact as a fail-closed contract
86	    # violation. (test_failures_summary was the original example; ADR-055 §9
87	    # since made it `required: true` — a summary is published on every terminal
88	    # verdict, so its absence IS a violation now.)
89	    local paths
90	    paths="$(_registry_output_path_rows "$manifest")"
91	
92	    [[ -z "$paths" ]] && return 0
93	
94	    local missing=0
95	    local raw_path raw_primary resolved _violation _event
96	    while IFS=$'\t' read -r raw_path raw_primary; do
97	        [[ -z "$raw_path" ]] && continue
98	        resolved="$(_registry_resolve_output_path "$raw_path" "$state_dir" "$artifact_dir")"
99	
100	        # An absent output always violates; a zero-byte one violates unless the
101	        # plugin declared the empty-diff capability AND this is not its primary.
102	        _violation=""
103	        if [[ ! -e "$resolved" ]]; then
104	            _violation="absent"
105	            _event="plugin.artifact.missing"
106	        elif [[ ! -s "$resolved" ]] &&
107	             ! { [[ "$empty_diff_ok" == "true" ]] && [[ "$raw_primary" != "true" ]]; }; then
108	            _violation="empty"
109	            _event="plugin.artifact.empty"
110	        fi
111	
112	        if [[ -n "$_violation" && "$probe" == "probe" ]]; then
113	            return 1
114	        fi

522	        # #2333: the group leader exiting does not mean its group members did.
523	        # A child that ignored TERM would survive if the watchdog is cancelled before
524	        # it delivers KILL, so KILL the whole group now.
525	        kill -KILL -- -"$_lc_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
526	        declare -F zbuild_pg_kill >/dev/null 2>&1 && zbuild_pg_kill "$_lc_wd_pid" 1 2>/dev/null || true
527	        wait "$_lc_wd_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
528	        if (( rc == 143 || rc == 137 )); then
529	            emit_event "plugin.run.timed_out" "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind" \
530	                "stage=${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" "timeout_s=${_lc_hook_to}" \
531	                "disposition=timed_out" 2>/dev/null || true
532	        fi
533	    else
534	        (
535	            # shellcheck disable=SC1090
536	            source "$plugin_sh"
537	            if declare -F "$hook_fn" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
538	                "$hook_fn" "$@"
539	            else
540	                echo "plugin_hook_call: function $hook_fn not defined in $plugin_sh" >&2
541	                exit 1
542	            fi
543	        )
544	        rc=$?
545	    fi
546	
547	    if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then
548	        # #288: after a successful `run`, verify the plugin actually produced
549	        # the artifacts it declared. Absent evidence IS blocking evidence —
550	        # emit synthetic findings for each missing output and surface the
551	        # failure as a non-zero hook exit so the caller can react.
552	        if [[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]]; then
553	            # Per ADR-001 hook signature: $@ after shift 2 is (stage_id, state_file, ...).
554	            local stage_arg="${1:-}"
555	            local state_file_arg="${2:-}"
556	            # #2252: a stage that SAYS it did not finish (timed_out, out_of_turns,
557	            # interrupted) is expected to be missing outputs — failing it for them
558	            # overwrote its retryable word with `broken` and halted the run
559	            # (#1844: design timed out, and the run ended instead of retrying).
560	            # Its own word stands; the retry rule decides what happens next.
561	            # Read the stage's word only when an output IS missing (a quiet
562	            # probe first): the read costs several jq calls per dispatch, and a
563	            # probe that passes means there is nothing for the full check to say.
564	            local _lcr_state="" _lcr_contract="" _lcr_verdict="" _lcr_disp="" _lcr_reason="" \
565	                  _lcr_viol="" _lcr_path="" _lcr_present="" _lc_unfinished="" _lc_missing=0
566	            scan_plugin_outputs "$plugin_dir" "$state_file_arg" "$stage_arg" probe 2>/dev/null || _lc_missing=1
567	            if (( _lc_missing )) && declare -F _verdict_read_result >/dev/null 2>&1 \
568	                    && declare -F disposition_unfinished >/dev/null 2>&1 \
569	                    && [[ -n "$state_file_arg" ]]; then
570	                _verdict_read_result "$(dirname "$state_file_arg")" "$manifest" "$stage_arg" 0 _lcr 2>/dev/null || true
571	                disposition_unfinished "${_lcr_disp:-}" && _lc_unfinished="$_lcr_disp"
572	            fi
573	            if [[ -n "$_lc_unfinished" ]]; then
574	                emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.artifact_check_skipped" "plugin=$plugin_id" \
575	                    "kind=$kind" "disposition=$_lc_unfinished"
576	            elif (( _lc_missing )) && ! scan_plugin_outputs "$plugin_dir" "$state_file_arg" "$stage_arg"; then
577	                emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.artifact_check_failed" \
578	                    "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind"
579	                # A dispatch that STARTED must also END. This arm and the
580	                # write-boundary arm below both `return 1` from inside the rc=0
581	                # branch, so neither reaches the `complete` emit nor the `else`
582	                # arm's `error` emit — the start was left without a partner and
583	                # the run's own log could not say which stage died (run
584	                # 33899683569: 54 start, 48 complete, 5 error). `reason=` is a
585	                # data field on an already-declared event name, so the event-NAME
586	                # set is unchanged and the sequence goldens are untouched.
587	                emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.error" "plugin=$plugin_id" \
588	                    "kind=$kind" "rc=1" "reason=artifact-check-failed"
589	                return 1
590	            fi
591	            # #1809 (ADR-058 C9): sweep for writes outside declared outputs and
592	            # engine-owned areas. Fail-open: unloaded module = write_boundary_check
593	            # undefined = this arm is unreachable.
594	            if declare -F write_boundary_check >/dev/null 2>&1; then
595	                _ZBUILD_WB_ACTION=""
596	                if ! write_boundary_check "$plugin_dir" "$state_file_arg" "$stage_arg" \
597	                        "${ZBUILD_MAP_ELEMENT:-}"; then
598	                    # See the artifact-check arm above: same missing-terminal
599	                    # defect. write_boundary_violation_recorded has already named
600	                    # the offending path on its own three channels; this event
601	                    # is what closes the start/end pair.
602	                    local _wb_reason="write-boundary-violation"
603	                    [[ "${_ZBUILD_WB_ACTION:-}" == "reverted" ]] && _wb_reason="write-boundary-reverted"
604	                    emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.error" "plugin=$plugin_id" \
605	                        "kind=$kind" "rc=1" "reason=$_wb_reason"
606	                    return 1
607	                fi
608	            fi
609	        fi
610	        emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.complete" "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind"
611	    else
612	        emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.error" "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind" "rc=$rc"
613	    fi
614	
615	    # #2183: keep THIS attempt's declared outputs before the next dispatch can
616	    # overwrite them. After the rc branches, so a FAILED attempt — the one whose
617	    # record matters most — is archived too. Fail-open by construction.
618	    if [[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]] && declare -F attempt_archive_outputs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
619	        attempt_archive_outputs "$plugin_dir" "${2:-}" "${1:-}" "$rc" "$_lc_outputs_before" 2>/dev/null || true
620	    fi
621	
622	    # #1823 (ADR-054 §4): the plugin's raw status passes through UNCHANGED, and
623	    # deliberately so during versioned coexistence. A v1 plugin has no result
624	    # field in which to say what its rc says — `plan`'s rc=10 IS its only way to
625	    # report `scope_too_large` — so narrowing here would destroy the meaning of
626	    # every unmigrated plugin at once. The narrowing is gated on the result
627	    # contract at the dispatch boundary instead (see cycle_dispatch_stage), and
628	    # becomes unconditional in #1850 when the last v1 reader is dropped.
629	    return $rc
630	}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
# ║  plugin-registry — lifecycle hook dispatch + fail-closed output scanner    ║
# ╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
#
# Split from registry.sh (#364). Owns the runtime dispatch path:
# `plugin_hook_call` (sources plugin.sh in an isolated subshell, applies
# pre-source tamper checks, calls the hook function, then verifies declared
# outputs) and `scan_plugin_outputs` (ADR-001 fail-closed artifact-presence
# scanner). Depends on yaml_get / verify_plugin_for_source from the other two
# split modules — sourced together via the registry.sh facade.
# Sourced library: inherits caller's pipefail settings; do not add set -euo pipefail.

[[ -n "${_ZBUILD_REGISTRY_LIFECYCLE_LOADED:-}" ]] && return 0
_ZBUILD_REGISTRY_LIFECYCLE_LOADED=1

# #1809 (ADR-058 C9): declared-output path resolution is shared with
# core/pipeline/write-boundary.sh so the artifact scanner and the write-boundary
# classifier can never disagree about where a declared output lives.
# shellcheck source=output-paths.sh
source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/output-paths.sh"
# shellcheck source=write-ownership.sh
source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/write-ownership.sh"
# shellcheck source=attempt-archive.sh
source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/attempt-archive.sh"
# shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/stage-dispatch-mark.sh
source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)/scripts/lib/stage-dispatch-mark.sh"

# ─── scan_plugin_outputs — fail-closed artifact-presence scanner (#288) ─────
# ADR-001 §Fail-closed scanner contract:
#   "If a plugin declares an output but no artifact exists at outputs[].path
#    after run completes with exit 0, the engine emits a synthetic blocking
#    finding."
# #1906 retired provides.artifact_type, which the original wording keyed on;
# outputs[].required is the single declaration the scan now honours.
#
# Arguments:
#   $1 — plugin_dir
#   $2 — state_file (so $state_dir / $artifacts_dir can substitute into paths)
#
# Returns:
#   0 if all declared outputs are present (or no outputs declared).
#   1 if any declared output is missing — and emits one
#      `plugin.artifact.missing` event per missing path.
#
# Path-template substitution (Phase 0.5): supports ${state_dir} and
# ${artifact_dir} / ${artifacts_dir}. Any other ${VAR} resolves from the work
# unit's exported environment (#1803) — per-member outputs such as review-lens's
# `lens-${ZBUILD_REVIEW_LENS_ID}.json` (ADR-047 §2) are only checkable once the
# element var is expanded. A var that is unset stays literal and fails the check.
scan_plugin_outputs() {
    local plugin_dir="$1"
    local state_file="${2:-}"
    local stage="${3:-}"
    # #2252: `probe` answers present-or-not with no events, findings or marker.
    local probe="${4:-}"
    local manifest="$plugin_dir/manifest.yaml"

    # No manifest, no outputs to scan — silently succeed.
    [[ ! -f "$manifest" ]] && return 0

    local plugin_id; plugin_id="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "id" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    local kind; kind="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "kind" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    # ADR-047 §4 capability flag: build legitimately writes a zero-byte diff.patch
    # when a turn changed no code. The exemption is deliberately narrow — it never
    # covers a `primary: true` output, so a stage cannot mask an empty verdict
    # artifact (e.g. build-summary.json) by declaring the flag in its own manifest.
    local empty_diff_ok; empty_diff_ok="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "capabilities.empty_diff_legitimate" 2>/dev/null || true)"

    # Compute substitution roots from state_file.
    local state_dir="" artifact_dir=""
    if [[ -n "$state_file" ]]; then
        state_dir="$(dirname "$state_file")"
        artifact_dir="${state_dir}/artifacts"
    fi

    # Pull outputs[].path entries from the manifest. yaml_get/yaml_get_list
    # don't model lists of objects, so grep the YAML directly. Format we
    # support (per ADR-001):
    #   outputs:
    #     - name: foo
    #       path: ${artifact_dir}/foo.json
    #       type: foo.json
    # #511 F2: respect `required: false` on outputs. Without this, the scanner
    # would flag a legitimately optional artifact as a fail-closed contract
    # violation. (test_failures_summary was the original example; ADR-055 §9
    # since made it `required: true` — a summary is published on every terminal
    # verdict, so its absence IS a violation now.)
    local paths
    paths="$(_registry_output_path_rows "$manifest")"

    [[ -z "$paths" ]] && return 0

    local missing=0
    local raw_path raw_primary resolved _violation _event
    while IFS=$'\t' read -r raw_path raw_primary; do
        [[ -z "$raw_path" ]] && continue
        resolved="$(_registry_resolve_output_path "$raw_path" "$state_dir" "$artifact_dir")"

        # An absent output always violates; a zero-byte one violates unless the
        # plugin declared the empty-diff capability AND this is not its primary.
        _violation=""
        if [[ ! -e "$resolved" ]]; then
            _violation="absent"
            _event="plugin.artifact.missing"
        elif [[ ! -s "$resolved" ]] &&
             ! { [[ "$empty_diff_ok" == "true" ]] && [[ "$raw_primary" != "true" ]]; }; then
            _violation="empty"
            _event="plugin.artifact.empty"
        fi

        if [[ -n "$_violation" && "$probe" == "probe" ]]; then
            return 1
        fi
        if [[ -n "$_violation" ]]; then
            if [[ "$_violation" == "absent" ]]; then
                error "scan_plugin_outputs: plugin=$plugin_id declared output missing: $resolved (template: $raw_path)"
            else
                error "scan_plugin_outputs: plugin=$plugin_id declared output is empty (zero bytes): $resolved (template: $raw_path)"
            fi
            emit_event "$_event" \
                "plugin=$plugin_id" \
                "kind=$kind" \
                "expected_path=$resolved" \
                "template=$raw_path"
            # ADR-001 §Fail-closed contract: emit plugin.contract.violated and write
            # synthetic blocking findings.json so the output stage can surface the violation.
            local _stage_id="${stage:-${plugin_id}}"
            emit_event "plugin.contract.violated" \
                "stage=$_stage_id" \
                "plugin=$plugin_id" \
                "expected_path=$resolved" \
                "reason=artifact_missing_or_empty"
            if [[ -n "$state_dir" ]]; then
                mkdir -p "${state_dir}/artifacts"
                local _findings_file="${state_dir}/artifacts/${_stage_id}-${plugin_id}-contract-violated-findings.json"
                jq -n \
                    --arg stage "$_stage_id" \
                    --arg plugin "$plugin_id" \
                    --arg path "$resolved" \
                    --arg violation "$_violation" \
                    '{
                        schema_version: 1,
                        findings: [{
                            id: "artifact-contract-violated",
                            title: ("Plugin contract violated: " + $plugin +
                                    (if $violation == "empty"
                                     then " wrote an empty (zero-byte) required output"
                                     else " declared a required output but wrote no artifact" end)),
                            severity: "blocking",
                            stage: $stage,
                            plugin: $plugin,
                            detail: ("Expected artifact at: " + $path)
                        }]
                    }' > "$_findings_file" 2>/dev/null || true
                # #1809: file-backed marker so runner_read_stage_disposition (a separate
                # process under map:) can detect the violation and return broken.
                mkdir -p "${state_dir}/runtime"
                touch "${state_dir}/runtime/artifact-contract-violated" 2>/dev/null || true
            fi
            missing=$((missing + 1))
        fi
    done <<< "$paths"

    return $((missing > 0))
}

# ─── _lc_owned_by_others_deny <state_dir> <stage> (#2189) ────────────────────
# One absolute path per line: every file a stage OTHER than <stage> reported
# owning (artifacts/stage-reports.json). Empty when nothing is owned.
_lc_owned_by_others_deny() {
    local rec="${1:-}/artifacts/stage-reports.json" me="${2:-}"
    [[ -s "$rec" ]] || return 0
    # Read without a fork: nothing owned (most runs) needs no jq at all.
    local _body; _body="$(<"$rec")"
    [[ "$_body" == *'"owned_files"'* ]] || return 0
    jq -r --arg me "$me" --arg root "${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-.}" '
        [(.owned_files // {}) | to_entries[] | select(.key != $me) | .value[] | "\($root)/\(.)"]
        | unique[]' <<< "$_body" 2>/dev/null
}

# ─── plugin_hook_call ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Source the plugin's plugin.sh and call a lifecycle hook by name.
# Plugin functions are isolated by sub-shell to prevent namespace pollution.
plugin_hook_call() {
    local plugin_dir="$1"
    local hook_name="$2"   # run | cleanup (or kind-specific)
    shift 2
    local manifest="$plugin_dir/manifest.yaml"
    local plugin_sh="$plugin_dir/plugin.sh"

    # ADR-068 §8: mark when this run of the stage started, FIRST — before any
    # refusal below can return — so a run that writes no result, refused or
    # not, is never credited with the previous run's (stage_result_is_current).
    [[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]] && stage_dispatch_mark "${2:-}" "${1:-}"

    if [[ ! -f "$plugin_sh" ]]; then
        error "plugin_hook_call: plugin.sh missing: $plugin_sh"
        return 1
    fi

    local plugin_id; plugin_id="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "id")"
    local kind; kind="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "kind")"

    # ADR-054 §3 (#1862): the engine states, for exactly the span of one
    # dispatch, which stage this is and which plugin serves it.
    #
    # A plugin IS self-defining about what it is — plugin-bootstrap.sh resolves
    # _ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR from its own BASH_SOURCE, and 18 plugins do. It can
    # never be self-defining about which STAGE it is: `review_lenses`
    # (simple.yaml) is served by plugin `review-lens` via role `review_lens` —
    # three namespaces the template alone maps, and under `map:` all six lens
    # members receive that one stage name. Everything keyed to the flow (the
    # timeline, stage_statuses, the per-stage router knobs) needs the stage
    # name; introspection can only ever yield the plugin id.
    #
    # `local -x`, not `export`, for three reasons: it reaches the emit_event
    # calls below, which fire OUTSIDE the plugin subshell (the blank envelope
    # .plugin/.kind of #1705); it reaches the subshell and anything it spawns;
    # and it unsets on return, so stage N's identity cannot bleed into stage
    # N+1 — a plain export would trade a blank field for a stale one.
    #
    # This is the only site that reaches all four dispatch arms. The `map:` arm
    # runs a generated standalone script (strategies/common.sh) the runner
    # cannot export into — but plugin_hook_call is its last line.
    #
    # ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT is deliberately NOT set: it is an operator override
    # every reader spells `${ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT:-<default>}`, and ADR-024 /
    # persona-resolve.sh forbid relying on it as a root. Derive from
    # ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR instead.
    #
    # Stage id is $1 post-shift for both hooks — run(stage_id, state_file, ...)
    # and cleanup(stage_id, state_file, scope), ADR-054 §2. Same assumption
    # scan_plugin_outputs already makes below.
    #
    # `:-` is deliberate and deliberately unlike `stage_arg="${1:-}"` below: an
    # empty $1 keeps the ambient stage rather than blanking it. A caller with no
    # stage to name must not erase the one its own caller established — the
    # throttle marker's path is keyed on this value and is written inside the
    # dispatch but read outside it (router-rc-classify.sh:154), so a blank here
    # would split the key across the boundary. scan_plugin_outputs has no such
    # cross-boundary reader and wants the literal argument.
    local -x ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE="${1:-${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}}"
    # #1706 (ADR-054 §3.1): the unit's own name — the stage, or <stage>.<element>
    # for a map member — for this dispatch only. The element is consumed here, so
    # a stage dispatched from inside the member is named by its own stage.
    local -x ZBUILD_UNIT="${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE}${ZBUILD_UNIT_ELEMENT:+.${ZBUILD_UNIT_ELEMENT}}"
    local -x ZBUILD_UNIT_ELEMENT=""
    local -x ZBUILD_PLUGIN="$plugin_id"
    local -x ZBUILD_PLUGIN_KIND="$kind"
    local -x ZBUILD_PLUGIN_DIR="$plugin_dir"

    # ADR-058 §2 (#1918): the engine states WHERE this stage may write, for
    # exactly the span of one dispatch. #1809 makes a declared output a write
    # boundary; a boundary cannot be enforced until the permitted areas are
    # defined, and the per-stage scratch area did not exist at all.
    #
    # Same site and same `local -x` as the identity block above, for the same
    # reasons: it is the only site reaching all four dispatch arms (the `map:`
    # arm runs a generated standalone script the runner cannot export into, and
    # this call is that script's last line), and `local -x` restores the prior
    # value AND the prior export attribute on return, so stage N's scratch
    # cannot bleed into stage N+1 and the test harness's sandboxed
    # ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR (scripts/lib/test-helpers.sh) comes back intact.
    #
    # Guarded on `$2` being an ABSOLUTE path — the state_file, post-shift, per
    # ADR-054 §2, the same argument scan_plugin_outputs reads below.
    #
    # Absolute, not merely non-empty, and the difference is load-bearing.
    # `dirname` of a bare relative name is `.`, and by the time a stage
    # dispatches, the runner has cd'd into the RUN'S WORKTREE (ADR-052) — so a
    # relative state_file would put `scratch/` and `artifacts/` inside the
    # repository under change. That is the exact leak this block exists to close,
    # reintroduced by the block itself.
    #
    # It cannot happen from the engine: runner.sh absolutizes state_dir "BEFORE
    # anything derives a path from state_dir" precisely so no caller has to think
    # about this (ADR-052, #1640). A relative or empty `$2` therefore means an
    # ad-hoc caller — the `plugin_hook_call … ""` of
    # tests/unit/plugin-lifecycle-event-balance-test.sh, or the positional
    # `… "arg1" "arg2"` of tests/integration/core-plugin-registry-test.sh — which
    # has no job folder to be inside and must reach the plugin with the
    # environment it has today.
    #
    # Setting TMPDIR is the load-bearing part. scripts/lib/env-scrub.sh
    # wildcard-unsets every ZBUILD_* before each model spawn — with the
    # unset-until-gone loop #1873 added specifically to defeat `local -x`
    # layering at this seam — while TMPDIR is explicitly PRESERVED. It is
    # therefore the only channel that reaches the model. Redirecting it puts the
    # model's own temp writes in bounds and relocates every `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}`
    # consumer in the engine and the plugins with zero plugin edits.
    #
    # ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR is a definition, not a leak fix: the gate plugins test
    # for a live state file first and only fall back to temp when invoked
    # ad-hoc, so their outputs land correctly today. What changes is that the
    # plugin's own fallback and scan_plugin_outputs' `${artifact_dir}`
    # substitution below become the same directory BY CONSTRUCTION, instead of
    # two independent derivations that a caller can silently split.
    if [[ "${2:-}" == /* ]]; then
        local _ws_state_dir; _ws_state_dir="$(dirname "$2")"
        local -x ZBUILD_ARTIFACT_DIR="${_ws_state_dir}/artifacts"

        # #2022: the acceptance TESTFILES belong to the stage that AUTHORS them.
        # Every other spawn is denied Edit() on them, so build cannot rewrite an
        # assertion to agree with its own implementation. Derived from the role
        # the plugin declares, never from a stage id: naming `build` here would
        # be a stage naming a stage, the shape #1767 removed from routing.
        # core/router/permissions.sh renders the rules; the decision is here.
        local -x ZBUILD_PERMISSION_DENY_EDIT=""
        # #2170: `$1` here is the STAGE ID — the function `shift 2`s its
        # plugin_dir/hook_name arguments away above. Looked up on the stage id
        # the role was always empty, so the author was denied its own testfiles
        # (invisible while the rule rendered as `Edit(/abs)`, #2163).
        # #2189: files ANOTHER stage reported owning (test-author reports the
        # testfiles it authored) — from the run's stage-reports record, never
        # design.md by path and never a role name. The owner is not denied.
        ZBUILD_PERMISSION_DENY_EDIT+="$(_lc_owned_by_others_deny "$_ws_state_dir" "${1:-}")"
        [[ -n "$ZBUILD_PERMISSION_DENY_EDIT" ]] && ZBUILD_PERMISSION_DENY_EDIT+=$'\n'

        # #2174: write ownership from the manifests (write-ownership.sh) —
        # other plugins' declared outputs, and the repo unless declared.
        _lc_other_outputs_deny "$plugin_dir" "$_ws_state_dir"   # parent shell: fills the memo
        ZBUILD_PERMISSION_DENY_EDIT+="$_LC_DENY_OUT"
        local _lc_wr; _lc_wr="$(manifest_index_get "$manifest" capabilities.writes_repository 2>/dev/null)" \
            || _lc_wr="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "capabilities.writes_repository" 2>/dev/null || true)"
        if [[ "${_lc_wr%$'\n'}" != "true" ]]; then
            _lc_repo_entries_deny "${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-.}"
            ZBUILD_PERMISSION_DENY_EDIT+="$_LC_DENY_OUT"
        fi

        if ! declare -F stage_scratch_ensure >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            # shellcheck source=../pipeline/stage-scratch.sh
            source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../pipeline" && pwd)/stage-scratch.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
        fi
        if declare -F stage_scratch_ensure >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            local _ws_scratch
            # Fail-open: an unnameable stage or an uncreatable directory leaves
            # both vars unset and every consumer on the fallback it has today.
            # A stage must not be refused dispatch because scratch was
            # unavailable — that would make a diagnostic convenience a new way
            # for a run to die.
            if _ws_scratch="$(stage_scratch_ensure "$_ws_state_dir" "${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" "${ZBUILD_MAP_ELEMENT:-}" 2>/dev/null)" \
               && [[ -n "$_ws_scratch" ]]; then
                local -x ZBUILD_STAGE_SCRATCH="$_ws_scratch"
                local -x TMPDIR="$_ws_scratch"
            fi
        fi

        # #2024: this seam records that a stage STARTED. It does not record a
        # process group, and the distinction is the whole point.
        #
        # It used to write `<stage>.pgid` from `$$`, which conflated two jobs.
        # As a process handle it was inert: a stage is a bash function call, so
        # no group exists at this seam and `$$` names the ENGINE's group, which
        # teardown then skipped — correctly, since signalling your own group
        # takes the runner down. But as a STARTED MARKER it was load-bearing:
        # `stage_statuses` is written only when a stage completes, so a stage
        # killed mid-flight is known to teardown by this file alone.
        #
        # One file could not honestly be both. Groups are registered by whoever
        # creates one (zbuild_pg_register); this writes `<stage>.started`, and
        # nothing reads it as a pgid. Do not reinstate a `.pgid` write here: any
        # pgid observable at dispatch cannot be signalled from inside the run.
        if [[ "$hook_name" == "run" && -n "${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" ]]; then
            local _st_dir="${_ws_state_dir}/runtime/stages"
            if mkdir -p "$_st_dir" 2>/dev/null; then
                # One path component, so no stage name can climb out of runtime/.
                local _st_key="${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE//[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/_}"
                # Fail-open: a stage is never refused dispatch over bookkeeping.
                : > "${_st_dir}/${_st_key}.started" 2>/dev/null || true
            fi
        fi

        # #1809 (ADR-058 C9): load the write-boundary enforcer lazily, same
        # pattern as stage-scratch.sh above. Fail-open: an unloadable module
        # leaves the mark unset and write_boundary_check returns 0 immediately.
        if ! declare -F write_boundary_mark >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            # shellcheck source=../pipeline/write-boundary.sh
            source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../pipeline" && pwd)/write-boundary.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
        fi
    fi

    # ADR-055 / ADR-067 §8 (amended): every stage gets the same three blocks —
    # what comes from the repository, the previous work, and the rules for the
    # stage — and the index of every stage's latest output, its own included.
    # Nothing is checked against what a stage "needs": there is no such list, and
    # a stage that finds something it needs missing says so in its own result.
    #
    # This is the only site reaching all four dispatch arms (the `map:` arm runs
    # a generated standalone script the runner cannot export into, and this call
    # is that script's last line), and `local -x` unsets on return so stage N's
    # blocks cannot bleed into stage N+1.
    #
    # plugins_root is derived from plugin_dir (plugins/<kind>/<id>/), not read
    # from ZBUILD_PLUGINS_ROOT — ADR-024 / persona-resolve.sh forbid relying on
    # that override as a root.
    if [[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]]; then
        if ! declare -F _inputs_resolve_stage >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            # shellcheck source=../pipeline/input-resolve.sh
            source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../pipeline" && pwd)/input-resolve.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
        fi
        if ! declare -F stage_blocks_write >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            # shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/stage-prompt.sh
            source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)/scripts/lib/stage-prompt.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
        fi
        local _ir_proot; _ir_proot="$(cd "$plugin_dir/../.." 2>/dev/null && pwd)"
        local _ir_state="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"
        if [[ -n "$_ir_state" && -n "${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" ]] && declare -F _inputs_resolve_stage >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            local -x ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS ZBUILD_STAGE_BLOCKS
            # Built here, in this shell, so the two readers below — each in its
            # own subshell — share one producer index instead of each building it.
            _inputs_build_producer_index "$_ir_proot" "$_ir_state" 2>/dev/null || true
            ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS="$(_inputs_resolve_stage "$ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE" "$_ir_proot" "$_ir_state" 2>/dev/null || true)"
            if declare -F stage_blocks_write >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                local _sb_repo="${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)}"
                ZBUILD_STAGE_BLOCKS="$(stage_blocks_write "$ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE" "$_ir_state" "$manifest" \
                    "$_ir_proot" "$ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS" "$_sb_repo" 2>/dev/null || true)"
                # What Previous work carried, so a run's record says what each
                # stage was given (#2124).
                if [[ -s "${ZBUILD_STAGE_BLOCKS:-}/previous-work.md" ]]; then
                    local _pw_n=0 _pw_f=0 _pw_l
                    while IFS= read -r _pw_l; do
                        [[ "$_pw_l" == "### "*" (verdict: "* ]] || continue
                        _pw_n=$((_pw_n + 1))
                        [[ "$_pw_l" == *"(verdict: fail)"* || "$_pw_l" == *"(verdict: failed)"* ]] && _pw_f=$((_pw_f + 1))
                    done < "$ZBUILD_STAGE_BLOCKS/previous-work.md"
                    emit_event "stage.previous_work.written" "stage=$ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE" \
                        "stages=$_pw_n" "failing=$_pw_f" 2>/dev/null || true
                fi
            fi
        fi
    fi

    local hook_fn; hook_fn="$(yaml_get "$manifest" "hooks.$hook_name")"
    if [[ -z "$hook_fn" ]]; then
        if [[ "$hook_name" == "cleanup" ]]; then
            # #1823 (ADR-054 §4): an absent OPTIONAL hook had nothing to do and
            # did it — rc 0. The absence is not lost: it rides
            # `plugin.cleanup.absent`, a declared channel, which is what #1828's
            # own acceptance asked for ("distinguishable in the engine's
            # RECORDS"). ADR-056 additionally returned rc=3 for this, justified
            # against ADR-001's "0=ok, 1=recoverable, 2=fatal" — the very table
            # ADR-054 §4 supersedes. Nothing in the engine ever read it.
            #
            # Consumers that need to tell "skipped" from "ran cleanly" — #1829's
            # teardown dispatch and #1830's teardown stage — read the event.
            # Two channels carrying one fact is the defect this contract exists
            # to end, and the rc is the one that cannot be enforced.
            emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.absent" "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind"
            return 0
        fi
        # Absent required hook: emit refused event and fail.
        emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.refused" "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind" "reason=hook-not-declared"
        return 1
    fi

    # Pre-source tamper check (#290). Honors ZBUILD_STRICT_PLUGIN_LOCK.
    if ! verify_plugin_for_source "$manifest"; then
        emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.refused" "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind" "reason=lockfile-mismatch"
        return 1
    fi

    # #1809 (ADR-058 C9): mark the dispatch start so write_boundary_check can
    # find files written during this dispatch. Fail-open: missing function = no-op.
    if declare -F write_boundary_mark >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        # Keyed on stage + map element so nested, map and parallel dispatches
        # against one state file do not share (and re-stamp) one window.
        write_boundary_mark "${2:-}" "${1:-}" "${ZBUILD_MAP_ELEMENT:-}" || true
    fi

    # #2186: what the declared outputs were before this run, so the attempt
    # record can say which ones the run actually changed. Fail-open.
    local _lc_outputs_before=""
    if [[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]] && declare -F attempt_outputs_fingerprint >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        _lc_outputs_before="$(attempt_outputs_fingerprint "$plugin_dir" "${2:-}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    fi

    emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.start" "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind"

    # Run in a subshell to isolate plugin's variables/functions.
    # For the "run" hook: arm a per-dispatch watchdog so a hung stage is killed at
    # stage_timeout_s (issue #1801, SPEC-1/SPEC-2). Precedence: template
    # _TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_<stage> > ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S env > 5400 s default.
    local rc=0
    if [[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]]; then
        if ! declare -F zbuild_pg_kill >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)/scripts/lib/proc-group.sh" 2>/dev/null || true
        fi
        local _lc_stage_safe="${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE//-/_}"
        local _lc_to_var="_TPL_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S_${_lc_stage_safe}"
        local _lc_hook_to="${!_lc_to_var:-}"
        [[ "$_lc_hook_to" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_lc_hook_to" -gt 0 ]] || _lc_hook_to="${ZBUILD_STAGE_TIMEOUT_S:-5400}"
        [[ "$_lc_hook_to" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_lc_hook_to" -gt 0 ]] || _lc_hook_to=5400
        local _lc_hook_pid _lc_wd_pid _lc_m_before=0
        [[ "$-" == *m* ]] && _lc_m_before=1
        set -m
        (
            # Always clear monitor mode: the hook subshell is already in its own
            # process group (created by set -m + & above). Any background job the
            # hook spawns must stay in that group so kill -KILL -- -<pgid> reaches
            # them. If the caller had set -m (e.g. _runner_dispatch_always_run's
            # outer subshell), the hook would inherit it and its children would get
            # their own groups, escaping the KILL (#2333 SPEC-6b).
            set +m
            # shellcheck disable=SC1090
            source "$plugin_sh"
            if declare -F "$hook_fn" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                "$hook_fn" "$@"
            else
                echo "plugin_hook_call: function $hook_fn not defined in $plugin_sh" >&2
                exit 1
            fi
        ) &
        _lc_hook_pid=$!
        ( set +m; sleep "$_lc_hook_to"; zbuild_pg_kill "$_lc_hook_pid" 10 2>/dev/null || true ) &
        _lc_wd_pid=$!
        set +m
        # Restore runner's monitor mode: set +m above always clears it, even when
        # ZBUILD_RUNNER_JOB_CONTROL=1 had it enabled before this call.
        (( _lc_m_before == 1 )) && set -m
        wait "$_lc_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null; rc=$?
        # #2333: the group leader exiting does not mean its group members did.
        # A child that ignored TERM would survive if the watchdog is cancelled before
        # it delivers KILL, so KILL the whole group now.
        kill -KILL -- -"$_lc_hook_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
        declare -F zbuild_pg_kill >/dev/null 2>&1 && zbuild_pg_kill "$_lc_wd_pid" 1 2>/dev/null || true
        wait "$_lc_wd_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
        if (( rc == 143 || rc == 137 )); then
            emit_event "plugin.run.timed_out" "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind" \
                "stage=${ZBUILD_CURRENT_STAGE:-}" "timeout_s=${_lc_hook_to}" \
                "disposition=timed_out" 2>/dev/null || true
        fi
    else
        (
            # shellcheck disable=SC1090
            source "$plugin_sh"
            if declare -F "$hook_fn" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                "$hook_fn" "$@"
            else
                echo "plugin_hook_call: function $hook_fn not defined in $plugin_sh" >&2
                exit 1
            fi
        )
        rc=$?
    fi

    if [[ $rc -eq 0 ]]; then
        # #288: after a successful `run`, verify the plugin actually produced
        # the artifacts it declared. Absent evidence IS blocking evidence —
        # emit synthetic findings for each missing output and surface the
        # failure as a non-zero hook exit so the caller can react.
        if [[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]]; then
            # Per ADR-001 hook signature: $@ after shift 2 is (stage_id, state_file, ...).
            local stage_arg="${1:-}"
            local state_file_arg="${2:-}"
            # #2252: a stage that SAYS it did not finish (timed_out, out_of_turns,
            # interrupted) is expected to be missing outputs — failing it for them
            # overwrote its retryable word with `broken` and halted the run
            # (#1844: design timed out, and the run ended instead of retrying).
            # Its own word stands; the retry rule decides what happens next.
            # Read the stage's word only when an output IS missing (a quiet
            # probe first): the read costs several jq calls per dispatch, and a
            # probe that passes means there is nothing for the full check to say.
            local _lcr_state="" _lcr_contract="" _lcr_verdict="" _lcr_disp="" _lcr_reason="" \
                  _lcr_viol="" _lcr_path="" _lcr_present="" _lc_unfinished="" _lc_missing=0
            scan_plugin_outputs "$plugin_dir" "$state_file_arg" "$stage_arg" probe 2>/dev/null || _lc_missing=1
            if (( _lc_missing )) && declare -F _verdict_read_result >/dev/null 2>&1 \
                    && declare -F disposition_unfinished >/dev/null 2>&1 \
                    && [[ -n "$state_file_arg" ]]; then
                _verdict_read_result "$(dirname "$state_file_arg")" "$manifest" "$stage_arg" 0 _lcr 2>/dev/null || true
                disposition_unfinished "${_lcr_disp:-}" && _lc_unfinished="$_lcr_disp"
            fi
            if [[ -n "$_lc_unfinished" ]]; then
                emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.artifact_check_skipped" "plugin=$plugin_id" \
                    "kind=$kind" "disposition=$_lc_unfinished"
            elif (( _lc_missing )) && ! scan_plugin_outputs "$plugin_dir" "$state_file_arg" "$stage_arg"; then
                emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.artifact_check_failed" \
                    "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind"
                # A dispatch that STARTED must also END. This arm and the
                # write-boundary arm below both `return 1` from inside the rc=0
                # branch, so neither reaches the `complete` emit nor the `else`
                # arm's `error` emit — the start was left without a partner and
                # the run's own log could not say which stage died (run
                # 33899683569: 54 start, 48 complete, 5 error). `reason=` is a
                # data field on an already-declared event name, so the event-NAME
                # set is unchanged and the sequence goldens are untouched.
                emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.error" "plugin=$plugin_id" \
                    "kind=$kind" "rc=1" "reason=artifact-check-failed"
                return 1
            fi
            # #1809 (ADR-058 C9): sweep for writes outside declared outputs and
            # engine-owned areas. Fail-open: unloaded module = write_boundary_check
            # undefined = this arm is unreachable.
            if declare -F write_boundary_check >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                _ZBUILD_WB_ACTION=""
                if ! write_boundary_check "$plugin_dir" "$state_file_arg" "$stage_arg" \
                        "${ZBUILD_MAP_ELEMENT:-}"; then
                    # See the artifact-check arm above: same missing-terminal
                    # defect. write_boundary_violation_recorded has already named
                    # the offending path on its own three channels; this event
                    # is what closes the start/end pair.
                    local _wb_reason="write-boundary-violation"
                    [[ "${_ZBUILD_WB_ACTION:-}" == "reverted" ]] && _wb_reason="write-boundary-reverted"
                    emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.error" "plugin=$plugin_id" \
                        "kind=$kind" "rc=1" "reason=$_wb_reason"
                    return 1
                fi
            fi
        fi
        emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.complete" "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind"
    else
        emit_event "plugin.$hook_name.error" "plugin=$plugin_id" "kind=$kind" "rc=$rc"
    fi

    # #2183: keep THIS attempt's declared outputs before the next dispatch can
    # overwrite them. After the rc branches, so a FAILED attempt — the one whose
    # record matters most — is archived too. Fail-open by construction.
    if [[ "$hook_name" == "run" ]] && declare -F attempt_archive_outputs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        attempt_archive_outputs "$plugin_dir" "${2:-}" "${1:-}" "$rc" "$_lc_outputs_before" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi

    # #1823 (ADR-054 §4): the plugin's raw status passes through UNCHANGED, and
    # deliberately so during versioned coexistence. A v1 plugin has no result
    # field in which to say what its rc says — `plan`'s rc=10 IS its only way to
    # report `scope_too_large` — so narrowing here would destroy the meaning of
    # every unmigrated plugin at once. The narrowing is gated on the result
    # contract at the dispatch boundary instead (see cycle_dispatch_stage), and
    # becomes unconditional in #1850 when the last v1 reader is dropped.
    return $rc
}

147	# #1878: last reported snapshot-failure reason, so a static precondition is
148	# reported once rather than once per stage boundary.
149	_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON=""

151	# ─── _runner_retry_budget <stage> (#2187, was #1887's redispatch budget) ─────
152	# How many times a stage whose disposition says `retry` is re-dispatched. The
153	# word never carries a count: the template's per-stage `retry:` wins, then the
154	# ZBUILD_DISPOSITION_REDISPATCH knob, then the engine default 3. Capped at 5 —
155	# the cycle re-runs its members anyway, so this is not a budget for grinding.
156	# A value above the cap clamps to the cap; a non-number is ignored.
157	_runner_retry_budget() {
158	    local v=""
159	    if declare -F template_stage_retry >/dev/null 2>&1; then
160	        v="$(template_stage_retry "${1:-}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
161	    fi
162	    [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || v="${ZBUILD_DISPOSITION_REDISPATCH:-}"
163	    [[ "$v" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || v=3
164	    (( v > 5 )) && v=5
165	    printf '%s' "$v"
166	}

168	# ─── _runner_leaf_contract_halt <state_file> <stage> <reason> ───────────────
169	# A leaf stage whose v2 result the engine rejected ends the run; rc 0 when it
170	# did. A cycle already halts on this (#550); a leaf recorded `error` and went on,
171	# which is how #1835's run shipped a plan result with no `reason`. Safe ahead of
172	# #1798: a contract violation is a zBuild defect (ADR-054 §6 `broken`), never a
173	# transient failure, so this cannot turn a network hiccup into a dead run.
174	# Reads main()'s _runner_run_id / _runner_issue and sets its _runner_ended.
175	_runner_leaf_contract_halt() {
176	    local sf="$1" st="$2" why="${3:-}"
177	    [[ "$why" == contract_violation:* ]] || return 1
178	    _update_stage_status "$sf" "$st" "failed"
179	    _set_pipeline_status "$sf" "failed"
180	    eb_emit_event "stage.fail" "stage=$st" "reason=$why" 2>/dev/null || true
181	    eb_emit_event "pipeline.end" "status=failed" "stage=$st" "reason=$why" \
182	        "run_id=${_runner_run_id:-}" "issue=${_runner_issue:-}" 2>/dev/null || true
183	    _render_pipeline_end "failed" "$st"
184	    _runner_ended=true
185	    error "Stage $st wrote a result the engine rejects ($why) — a zBuild defect; the run stops here"
186	    return 0
187	}

189	# ─── _runner_leaf_verdict_halt <state_file> <stage> <class> <raw> ────────────
190	# #1798 (ADR-054 §4): a leaf stage that reports a failure ends the run; rc 0
191	# when it did. <class> is the classified verdict the runner already read
192	# (runner_read_stage_verdict: fail, or a structural word passed through);
193	# <raw> is the stage's own word, which the run's end names. A cycle acts on its
194	# members' verdicts; a leaf used to record one, pick a glyph from it and
195	# complete anyway. A template opts a stage out with `blocking: false`
196	# (ADR-013) — advisory by declaration, never by accident.
197	_runner_leaf_verdict_halt() {
198	    local sf="$1" st="$2" v="${3:-}" raw="${4:-}"
199	    case "$v" in
200	        fail|error|block|scope_violation|corrupt_diff) ;;
201	        *) return 1 ;;
202	    esac
203	    [[ "$(template_stage_blocking "$st" 2>/dev/null)" == "false" ]] && return 1
204	    [[ -n "$raw" && "$raw" != "missing" ]] || raw="$v"
205	    _update_stage_status "$sf" "$st" "failed"
206	    _zbuild_state_set_stage_verdict "$sf" "$st" "$v"
207	    _set_pipeline_status "$sf" "failed"
208	    # No `rc=` field: the stage exited 0, so a verdict-triggered stage.fail
209	    # carries the stage's word (`verdict=`) instead — as the contract halt
210	    # carries `reason=` alone. A consumer of stage.fail reads either shape.
211	    eb_emit_event "stage.fail" "stage=$st" "verdict=$raw" "reason=stage_failed:$raw" 2>/dev/null || true
212	    eb_emit_event "pipeline.end" "status=failed" "stage=$st" "reason=stage_failed:$raw" \
213	        "run_id=${_runner_run_id:-}" "issue=${_runner_issue:-}" 2>/dev/null || true
214	    _render_pipeline_end "failed" "$st"
215	    _runner_ended=true
216	    error "Stage $st reported $raw — the run stops here"
217	    return 0
218	}

220	# ─── _runner_attempt_made_progress <artifact_dir> <stage> <iter> (#2187) ─────
221	# Attempts are numbered from 1 (attempt-archive.sh writes n+1).
222	# rc 0 when the stage's LATEST attempt in this iteration changed any of its
223	# declared outputs (the #2186 attempt record), or when there is no record to
224	# judge by; rc 1 when every output it recorded came back unchanged or absent —
225	# retrying the same work would hit the same wall.
226	_runner_attempt_made_progress() {
227	    local base="${1:-}/attempts/${2//[^A-Za-z0-9_-]/_}" iter="${3:-0}"
228	    [[ -d "$base" ]] || return 0
229	    local latest="" n=0 d k
230	    for d in "$base"/iter-"$iter"-attempt-*; do
231	        [[ -f "$d/attempt.json" ]] || continue
232	        k="${d##*-attempt-}"
233	        [[ "$k" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
234	        (( k > n )) && { n="$k"; latest="$d/attempt.json"; }
235	    done
236	    [[ -n "$latest" ]] || return 0
237	    # #2252: the archive's own judgement of the WORK, when it made one.
238	    if jq -e 'has("progress")' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
239	        jq -e '.progress == true' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1
240	        return
241	    fi
242	    jq -e 'has("outputs") | not' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
243	    jq -e '[.outputs[]] | any(. == "changed")' "$latest" >/dev/null 2>&1
244	}

246	# ─── _runner_note_push_failure <stage> (#2187) ───────────────────────────────
247	# Report a failed stage-end push once per distinct reason, on the same channel
248	# and dedupe as a failed snapshot.
249	_runner_note_push_failure() {
250	    [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" == "failed" ]] || return 0
251	    [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-}" != "${_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON:-}" ]] || return 0
252	    _RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
253	    eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.failed" "stage=${1:-unknown}" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
254	        "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
255	    warn "stage-end push failed at stage '${1:-unknown}': ${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
256	}

258	# ─── _runner_push_work_branch <state_dir> <stage> (#2187) ────────────────────
259	# When the run has a work branch on origin (ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH — CI sets
260	# zbuild/issue-N-ci), push the run's commits to it at every stage end, so a new
261	# session can pick them up even if this runner dies. No changes, no save: only
262	# when HEAD carries commits past the run's baseline — and before intake has
263	# recorded that baseline the run has made none, so nothing is pushed (#1801 run
264	# 38290215955: the end of hydrate force-pushed main over the branch's earlier
265	# work). Advisory: a failure is reported, never fatal.
266	_runner_push_work_branch() {
267	    local _branch="${ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH:-}"
268	    [[ -n "$_branch" ]] || return 0
269	    local _repo="${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}"
270	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || _repo="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
271	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || return 0
272	    git -C "$_repo" remote get-url origin >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
273	    local _base="" _ahead
274	    [[ -f "${1:-}/intake-baseline-ref.txt" ]] && _base="$(cat "${1:-}/intake-baseline-ref.txt" 2>/dev/null || true)"
275	    [[ -n "$_base" ]] || return 0
276	    _ahead="$(git -C "$_repo" rev-list --count "$_base..HEAD" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
277	    [[ "$_ahead" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$_ahead" -gt 0 ]] || return 0
278	    local _err
279	    if _err="$(git -C "$_repo" push --force -q origin "HEAD:refs/heads/$_branch" 2>&1)"; then
280	        return 0
281	    fi
282	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
283	    _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="git push work branch $_branch failed: $(tr '\n' ' ' <<< "$_err" | cut -c1-300)"
284	    _runner_note_push_failure "${2:-unknown}"
285	    return 0
286	}

288	# ─── _runner_keep_head_on_branch <state_dir> <stage> (#2264) ─────────────────
289	# A model call can leave HEAD off the run branch; every later commit then lands
290	# on HEAD alone while the branch ref — which pr-open checks out and the post-run
291	# step pushes — falls behind. #1844 run 37066147994 lost its work that way. At
292	# every stage end, put HEAD back on the branch when that drops nothing, and say
293	# which stage left it off; when the two diverged, move nothing and say so.
294	_runner_keep_head_on_branch() {
295	    local _sd="${1:-}" _stage="${2:-unknown}" _branch=""
296	    [[ -f "$_sd/intake-branch.txt" ]] && read -r _branch 2>/dev/null < "$_sd/intake-branch.txt"
297	    _branch="${_branch//[[:space:]]/}"
298	    [[ -n "$_branch" ]] || return 0
299	    local _repo="${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}"
300	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || _repo="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || true)"
301	    [[ -n "$_repo" ]] || return 0
302	    zbuild_keep_head_on_branch "$_repo" "$_branch"
303	    case "$ZBUILD_HEAD_OUTCOME" in
304	        reattached)
305	            eb_emit_event "pipeline.head.reattached" "stage=$_stage" "branch=$_branch" \
306	                "was=$ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS" 2>/dev/null || true
307	            warn "stage '$_stage' left HEAD off the run branch ($ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS) — moved '$_branch' to HEAD" ;;
308	        diverged)
309	            eb_emit_event "pipeline.head.diverged" "stage=$_stage" "branch=$_branch" \
310	                "was=$ZBUILD_HEAD_WAS" 2>/dev/null || true
311	            warn "stage '$_stage' left HEAD off the run branch and the two diverged — '$_branch' not moved" ;;
312	    esac
313	    return 0
314	}

316	# ─── _runner_snapshot_artifacts <state_dir> <stage> (ADR-050, #1581/#1878) ───
317	# Snapshot the artifact area onto the state branch at a stage boundary, so a
318	# completed stage's work survives a mid-run crash/rate-limit and is available to
319	# the next run. Stage-agnostic (snapshots whatever files exist) and advisory —
320	# never blocks a run.
321	#
322	# #1878: ONE definition, called from every stage-completion site on the LIVE
323	# dispatch-unit path. It previously existed only inline in the legacy linear stage
324	# loop below — which no shipped template ever reaches (any cycle/map/parallel unit
325	# sets _run_dispatch_units=1, and every terminal branch of that block returns), so
326	# the snapshot was never invoked at all and the store was always empty. That is
327	# item 1 of #1807.
328	#
329	# #1878: also no longer swallows stderr. A snapshot that fails now says so, with
330	# the failing git operation named, instead of returning 1 into a `2>/dev/null`
331	# and leaving no trace anywhere.
332	_runner_snapshot_artifacts() {
333	    # $1 may be empty: the cycle-orchestrator call site is several frames from
334	    # main(), and relying on main()'s `state_dir` local reaching it through
335	    # dynamic scope is exactly the kind of implicit coupling that makes a call
336	    # site silently no-op. The runner exports the resolved per-run value at
337	    # runner.sh:1739, so fall back to that.
338	    local _snap_state_dir="${1:-}" _snap_stage="${2:-unknown}"
339	    [[ -n "$_snap_state_dir" ]] || _snap_state_dir="${ZBUILD_STATE_DIR:-}"
340	    [[ -n "$_snap_state_dir" ]] || return 0
341	    # Before the identity guard: a --goal or local run needs its branch kept too.
342	    _runner_keep_head_on_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
343	    # #1931: identity, not issue number. `issue > 0` excluded every --goal run
344	    # from the durable store, so nothing was ever snapshotted for one and the
345	    # push had nothing to send.
346	    _artifact_persist_has_identity "$_runner_issue" || return 0
347	
348	    _artifact_persist_snapshot "$_snap_state_dir" "$_runner_issue" || true
349	    case "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" in
350	        saved)
351	            eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.saved" \
352	                "stage=$_snap_stage" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
353	                "skipped=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_SKIPPED:-0}" 2>/dev/null || true
354	            ;;
355	        failed)
356	            # Loud, not fatal. This event is the whole point of #1878: the defect
357	            # went undiagnosed for the life of the feature because the failure had
358	            # no channel to surface on.
359	            #
360	            # Deduped on the reason. Most failures are a STATIC precondition — no
361	            # resolvable repository, a ref D/F conflict — so they recur identically
362	            # at every stage boundary. Reporting the first occurrence keeps the
363	            # signal; repeating it once per stage is noise that trains an operator
364	            # to ignore the event. A CHANGED reason is always reported.
365	            if [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-}" != "${_RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON:-}" ]]; then
366	                _RUNNER_LAST_SNAPSHOT_FAIL_REASON="${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
367	                eb_emit_event "artifact.snapshot.failed" \
368	                    "stage=$_snap_stage" "issue=$_runner_issue" \
369	                    "reason=${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}" 2>/dev/null || true
370	                warn "artifact snapshot failed at stage '$_snap_stage': ${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON:-unknown}"
371	            fi
372	            ;;
373	        # empty / unchanged are not failures and are not events: emitting
374	        # `saved` for them is precisely the lie this change removes.
375	        *) : ;;
376	    esac
377	    # #2187: push at the stage end, not only when the run ends — a run killed
378	    # mid-way (job ceiling, SIGKILL) otherwise loses everything since its start.
379	    # Only for a run that declares where its work goes (ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH;
380	    # the CI pipeline sets it). A plain local run — and every test — pushes
381	    # nothing here: tests have left state branches in real checkouts, and
382	    # this would put them on origin. The persist stage still pushes at the end.
383	    [[ -n "${ZBUILD_WORKSPACE_BRANCH:-}" ]] || return 0
384	    local _leak=""
385	    if _leak="$(_artifact_persist_find_secret "$_snap_state_dir/artifacts")"; then
386	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS="failed"
387	        _ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_REASON="refusing to push — artifact looks like it carries a credential (${_leak})"
388	        _runner_note_push_failure "$_snap_stage"
389	        # The scan covers the artifact area, not the working tree: the run's
390	        # code commits still go to the work branch.
391	        _runner_push_work_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
392	        return 0
393	    fi
394	    if [[ "${_ARTIFACT_PERSIST_LAST_STATUS:-}" == "saved" ]]; then
395	        _artifact_persist_push "$_runner_issue" "${ZBUILD_REPO_ROOT:-}" || true
396	        _runner_note_push_failure "$_snap_stage"
397	    fi
398	    _runner_push_work_branch "$_snap_state_dir" "$_snap_stage"
399	    return 0
400	}

402	# ─── stage-start time cache (#508) ───────────────────────────────────────────
403	# Populated immediately before _render_stage_divider for each stage; read at
404	# the ✓/✗ complete/fail sites to compute the duration suffix. assoc array so
405	# nested / out-of-order stages (none today, but safe) still resolve correctly.
406	declare -gA _RUNNER_STAGE_START_MS=()
407	
408	# ─── pipeline-wide start time cache (#525) ───────────────────────────────────
409	# Populated once at the top of main() right after _runner_run_id is sanitized
410	# (well before the EXIT trap installs) so every pipeline.end emit site — incl.
411	# preflight failure (L289) and the EXIT trap — can render a duration. Empty
412	# until set; readers degrade to "?s" on cache-miss (mirrors _runner_duration_token).
413	_RUNNER_PIPELINE_START_MS=""

415	# ─── _runner_now_ms (#508) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
416	# Millisecond wall clock. Honors ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_NOW_MS_OVERRIDE so goldens
417	# can pin the timestamp (same env var as stage-io.sh — single test contract;
418	# do NOT introduce a runner-specific override name). Non-numeric override is
419	# treated as unset (defensive: a stray export shouldn't crash the runner).
420	# Empty stdout on failure → caller renders "??:??:?? UTC" / "?s" — no crash.
421	_runner_now_ms() {
422	    local ovr="${ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_NOW_MS_OVERRIDE:-}"
423	    if [[ -n "$ovr" && "$ovr" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
424	        printf '%s' "$ovr"
425	        return 0
426	    fi
427	    if [[ -n "${EPOCHREALTIME:-}" ]]; then
428	        local us="${EPOCHREALTIME/./}"
429	        printf '%s' $(( 10#${us} / 1000 ))
430	        return 0
431	    fi
432	    printf '%s' "$(( ${EPOCHSECONDS:-$(date -u +%s)} * 1000 ))"
433	}

435	# ─── _runner_status_comment_spawn <state_dir> <events_jsonl> <repo_root> ─────
436	# #2131 (ADR-064): the live run-status comment is a SIDECAR that tails
437	# events.jsonl — the engine never renders GitHub markdown itself, it only
438	# starts an observer and stops it. Spawned here, in the runner, so a local
439	# `zbuild pipeline start --issue N` and the CI workflow share one code path
440	# (CI needs no extra step: GITHUB_TOKEN is already job-level env). Every
441	# gate that keeps a test's temp repo off GitHub lives in rsc_enabled; the
442	# harness also pins ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT=0. The sidecar's fd 3 is closed so
443	# it never holds the stage-io channel open.
444	_RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
445	_runner_status_comment_spawn() {
446	    local state_dir="$1" events_jsonl="$2" repo_root="${3:-$PWD}"
447	    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
448	    # The explicit kill switch leaves NO trace — not even a log line. The
449	    # parity golden lists every file in the state dir, and every test runs
450	    # with the switch on (run-tests.sh); a "disabled" file there would be
451	    # noise in every fixture for a fact the operator already knows.
452	    [[ "${ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT:-1}" == "0" ]] && return 0
453	    local lib="$_ZBUILD_ROOT/scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh"
454	    [[ -f "$lib" ]] || return 0
455	    # shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/run-status-comment.sh
456	    source "$lib" 2>/dev/null || return 0
457	    rsc_enabled "$state_dir" "$repo_root" || return 0
458	    local slug; slug="$(zbuild_repo_slug "$repo_root" 2>/dev/null || true)"
459	    ( exec 3>&- 2>/dev/null
460	      exec bash "$lib" --events "$events_jsonl" --state-dir "$state_dir" \
461	           --parent-pid $$ --slug "$slug" --issue "${ZBUILD_ISSUE:-0}" \
462	           --run-id "${ZBUILD_RUN_ID:-}" --repo-root "$repo_root" ) \
463	        </dev/null >>"$state_dir/status-comment.log" 2>&1 &
464	    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=$!
465	    return 0
466	}

468	# ─── _runner_status_comment_reap ─────────────────────────────────────────────
469	# Idempotent (clears the pid first) and rc-neutral (`return 0`, every line
470	# tolerant): it runs inside the EXIT trap under `set -e`, and the process exit
471	# status must never depend on GitHub. TERM, bounded wait, KILL backstop.
472	_runner_status_comment_reap() {
473	    local pid="${_RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID:-}"
474	    [[ -n "$pid" ]] || return 0
475	    _RUNNER_STATUS_COMMENT_PID=""
476	    if kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
477	        kill -TERM "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
478	        local i
479	        for (( i = 0; i < ${ZBUILD_STATUS_COMMENT_REAP_TIMEOUT:-45} * 10; i++ )); do
480	            kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || break
481	            sleep 0.1
482	        done
483	        kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null && kill -KILL "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
484	    fi
485	    wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
486	    return 0
487	}

489	# ─── _runner_now_short (#508) — HH:MM:SS UTC for stage banners ───────────────
490	# Returns ??:??:?? UTC when the underlying clock primitive yields nothing
491	# (defensive — the operator-visible banner still renders without crashing).
492	_runner_now_short() {
493	    local ms; ms="$(_runner_now_ms)"
494	    if [[ -z "$ms" || ! "$ms" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
495	        printf '??:??:?? UTC'
496	        return 0
497	    fi
498	    local sec=$(( ms / 1000 ))
499	    local out
500	    out="$(date -u -r "$sec" +'%H:%M:%S UTC' 2>/dev/null \
501	        || date -u -d "@$sec" +'%H:%M:%S UTC' 2>/dev/null \
502	        || printf '??:??:?? UTC')"
503	    printf '%s' "$out"
504	}

506	# ─── _runner_duration_token <stage> (#508) ───────────────────────────────────
507	# Format the elapsed duration since the start cache was populated. Mirrors
508	# stage-io.sh::_stage_io_render_duration's "<N.N>s" for sub-minute durations;
509	# for >= 60 s we use "<m>m<ss>s" so a slow stage doesn't render as "127.4s".
510	# Cache miss → "?s" (no crash).
511	_runner_duration_token() {
512	    local stage="$1"
513	    local start="${_RUNNER_STAGE_START_MS[$stage]:-}"
514	    if [[ -z "$start" || ! "$start" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
515	        printf '?s'
516	        return 0
517	    fi
518	    local now; now="$(_runner_now_ms)"
519	    if [[ -z "$now" || ! "$now" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
520	        printf '?s'
521	        return 0
522	    fi
523	    local ms=$(( now - start ))
524	    (( ms < 0 )) && ms=0
525	    if (( ms < 60000 )); then
526	        awk -v m="$ms" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1fs", m/1000}'
527	    else
528	        local total_s=$(( ms / 1000 ))
529	        local mins=$(( total_s / 60 ))
530	        local secs=$(( total_s % 60 ))
531	        printf '%dm%02ds' "$mins" "$secs"
532	    fi
533	}

535	# ─── _runner_export_scope_allowlist <state_dir> (ADR-043) ────────────────────
536	# Redaction by construction: the per-run scope allowlist, exported as
537	# ZBUILD_SCOPE_ALLOWLIST so route_to_model can redact without a plugin passing
538	# it. Called per-stage because nothing is reported before plan runs (empty then —
539	# harmless, the scope manifest is the base allowlist and this is purely ADDITIVE).
540	_runner_export_scope_allowlist() {
541	    local state_dir="$1"
542	    local rec="$state_dir/artifacts/stage-reports.json" csv=""
543	    # #2189: the scope files stages REPORTED (plan reports its files) — the
544	    # engine no longer reads plan.json by path.
545	    if [[ -s "$rec" ]]; then
546	        csv="$(jq -r '(.scope_files // []) | unique | join(",")' "$rec" 2>/dev/null || echo "")"
547	    fi
548	    # #1874: the shape floor is part of the scope — computed here, mechanically,
549	    # so build, redaction and shape-floor all read one list that already holds
550	    # the files a shape change owes. Memoised per scope: this runs every stage.
551	    if [[ -n "$csv" && "$csv" != "${_RUNNER_FLOOR_KEY:-}" ]]; then
552	        _RUNNER_FLOOR_KEY="$csv"; _RUNNER_FLOOR_CSV="$csv"
553	        if ! declare -F sf_scope_floor_files >/dev/null 2>&1; then
554	            # shellcheck source=../../scripts/lib/shape-floor.sh
