569	# ─── _runner_record_report <state_dir> <stage> <report-json> (#2189) ─────────
570	# Merge one dispatch's report into the run's record, artifacts/stage-reports.json
571	# (under artifacts/ so it is snapshotted and restored with the run): scope and
572	# wiring files are unioned; owned files are kept per reporting stage, so the
573	# deny list can exempt the owner. Engine setup reads THIS record — never a
574	# stage's artifact by name. Best-effort: a failed merge leaves the prior record.
575	# Parallel members record concurrently, so the read-merge-write holds a mkdir
576	# lock (portable; flock is absent on stock macOS) — else a sibling's merge is lost.
577	# A lock left by a killed holder is reclaimed after 10s.
578	_runner_record_report() {
579	    local state_dir="$1" stage="$2" report="${3:-}"
580	    [[ -n "$state_dir" && -n "$stage" && -n "$report" && "$report" != "{}" ]] || return 0
581	    # Most stages report none of the setup fields — skip the lock and the jq fork.
582	    [[ "$report" == *'"scope_files"'* || "$report" == *'"owned_files"'* \
583	        || "$report" == *'"wiring_files"'* ]] || return 0
584	    local rec="$state_dir/artifacts/stage-reports.json" tmp
585	    local lock="$state_dir/.stage-reports.lock" _tries=0
586	    [[ -d "$state_dir/artifacts" ]] || mkdir -p "$state_dir/artifacts" 2>/dev/null || return 0
587	    until mkdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null; do
588	        # A merge takes milliseconds; a lock held 10s belongs to a dead holder.
589	        if (( ++_tries > 200 )); then rmdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null; _tries=0; fi
590	        sleep 0.05
591	    done
592	    [[ -s "$rec" ]] || printf '{}' > "$rec"
593	    tmp="$rec.tmp.$BASHPID"
594	    if jq --arg s "$stage" --argjson r "$report" '
595	            .scope_files  = ((.scope_files  // []) + ($r.scope_files  // []) | unique)
596	          | .wiring_files = ((.wiring_files // []) + ($r.wiring_files // []) | unique)
597	          | if ($r.owned_files // null) != null
598	              then .owned_files = ((.owned_files // {}) + {($s): ($r.owned_files | unique)})
599	              else . end' "$rec" > "$tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
600	        mv -f "$tmp" "$rec"
601	    else
602	        rm -f "$tmp"
603	    fi
604	    rmdir "$lock" 2>/dev/null
605	    return 0
606	}

608	# ─── _runner_validate_leaf_resolvability <stages_arr_name> <plugins_root> ─────
609	# ADR-047 §5: the manifest-derived membership fence — the sole membership
610	# enforcement (the old hardcoded-roster fence is deleted, #1299). Every leaf in the
611	# resolved template flow must resolve to a plugin via resolve_stage_plugin
612	# (role-then-id, ADR-042); an unresolved leaf names the id.
613	#
614	# It is a CONTRACT check, so it is gated by the SAME ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR mode
615	# the inter-stage contract-validator uses (they must agree). Load-time membership
616	# enforcement is the ENFORCE-mode job; the opt-out modes (warn/off) skip it — so
617	# this preflight is a TRUE NO-OP whenever enforcement is off and never perturbs the
618	# mock-roster suites that drive runner.sh under warn (they resolve their leaves at
619	# dispatch via mocked plugin_hook_call, not through a real registry):
620	#   - enforce (default, real runs) / unset → ERROR fail-closed (rc=2). This is the
621	#     load-time guarantee that replaces the old canonical membership gate.
622	#   - warn / off (or any unknown mode)     → skip. Dispatch-time resolution
623	#     (resolve_stage_plugin in the stage loop) still fails a genuinely-missing
624	#     plugin mid-run — the backstop for opt-out runs.
625	# Takes the stage array BY NAME to avoid a subshell copy on read.
626	_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability() {
627	    local _arr_name="$1" plugins_root="$2"
628	    # Only enforce gates at load; warn/off/unknown are opt-outs → no-op. (The
629	    # default is enforce, matching contract-validator's default; unknown modes
630	    # degrade to non-enforce, exactly as contract-validator degrades them to warn.)
631	    [[ "${ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR:-enforce}" == "enforce" ]] || return 0
632	    # Validate the array name is a plain identifier before binding the nameref
633	    # below — never bind a name assembled from unvalidated input (Copilot #1290:
634	    # injection footgun). Callers pass a literal ("active_stages"), so a
635	    # non-identifier is a programming error, not runtime data.
636	    if [[ ! "$_arr_name" =~ ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ ]]; then
637	        error "_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: invalid array name '${_arr_name}'"
638	        return 1
639	    fi
640	    # bash errors on a nameref that resolves to itself; reject it with our own
641	    # message rather than a raw "circular name reference" from the shell.
642	    if [[ "$_arr_name" == "_stages" ]]; then
643	        error "_runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: array name '_stages' collides with the nameref"
644	        return 1
645	    fi
646	    # Warm the manifest cache in THIS shell before resolving anything. Every
647	    # resolution below reads manifests through `$( )`, and an associative-array
648	    # write inside a command substitution dies with that subshell — so a lazily
649	    # filled cache is never inherited (#1614, the reason yaml_cache_prewarm
650	    # exists and main() calls it at line ~1370).
651	    #
652	    # main() is not the only entry point. Tests source this file and call helpers
653	    # directly, never reaching that prewarm, and then every lookup forks awk:
654	    # template-resolvability-preflight-test.sh made 28,068 yaml_get calls with
655	    # ZERO cache hits, at real 150s / user 52s / sys 81s — kernel time 1.55x
656	    # user, which is process creation, not computation. Prewarming here took it
657	    # to 82.75s with sys 81s -> 45s.
658	    #
659	    # Here and not in setup_test_env: the prewarm costs 1.32s, and 570 test
660	    # files would pay ~747s for it to benefit the few that resolve plugins.
661	    # Measured before choosing the seam.
662	    #
663	    # Idempotent: a second call re-reads the same keys, which are now cache
664	    # hits. Cheap no-op in production, where main() has already warmed it.
665	    if declare -F yaml_cache_prewarm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
666	        yaml_cache_prewarm "$plugins_root"
667	    fi
668	    # Discovery too, for the same reason and in the same shell: it validates
669	    # every manifest on every call (~1.47s even with the yaml cache warm) and
670	    # runs once per leaf. 19 leaves x 2 templates was 38 full re-validations of
671	    # an unchanged tree.
672	    if declare -F discover_plugins >/dev/null 2>&1; then
673	        discover_plugins "$plugins_root" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
674	    fi
675	    local -n _stages="${_arr_name}"
676	    local _leaf _ok=1
677	    for _leaf in "${_stages[@]+"${_stages[@]}"}"; do
678	        [[ -z "$_leaf" ]] && continue
679	        # A cycle/parallel GROUP id is a composition operator, not a leaf, and is
680	        # not itself a plugin — its members are already flattened into the stage
681	        # list. Skip group ids (their _TPL_STAGE_TYPE_<id> is cycle|parallel).
682	        local _t_var="_TPL_STAGE_TYPE_${_leaf//-/_}"
683	        case "${!_t_var:-leaf}" in
684	            cycle|parallel) continue ;;
685	        esac
686	        if ! resolve_stage_plugin "$_leaf" "$plugins_root" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
687	            error "load_template: stage '${_leaf}' resolves to no plugin (ADR-047 §5: every leaf must resolve via role or id; add a plugin whose provides.role matches, or whose id is '${_leaf}')"
688	            _ok=0
689	        fi
690	    done
691	    [[ $_ok -eq 1 ]]
692	}

694	# ─── _runner_validate_startup_preflight [violation_fixture] (ADR-051 §warn-first) ──
695	# Aggregation SKELETON (#1318 / D1): owns the violations[]/fail_count collection,
696	# the render-all-at-once block (same pattern as _contract_validate_pipeline) and the
697	# warn/enforce/off mode dispatch. Separate gate from _runner_validate_leaf_
698	# resolvability — it covers non-contract elements the DAG validator does not address.
699	#
700	# It deliberately contributes NO checks of its own yet. The concrete producers land
701	# downstream, each against the discriminating fixtures #1605 pre-stages:
702	#   - persona-binding existence (PERSONA_MISSING) → #1320 (D3)
703	#   - requires.plugins resolution (PLUGIN_MISSING) → #1321 (D4)
704	# An earlier draft carried both checks here, untested; the requires.plugins one was
705	# an acknowledged approximation that raised spurious PLUGIN_MISSING for any entry
706	# naming an ordinary plugin. Shipping checks no test discriminates is the green-but-
707	# inert shape #1605 exists to prevent, so they were removed rather than carried.
708	#
709	# Deliberate divergence from _runner_validate_leaf_resolvability: the DEFAULT mode
710	# here is WARN (not enforce). This lands warn-first so operators see failures before
711	# enforcement is mandatory. Set ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=enforce to fail-closed.
712	# ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=off is a full no-op (skips all checks, emits nothing).
713	#
714	# The optional first argument is a synthetic violation fixture: it injects one
715	# pre-formed violation so the aggregation, rendering and mode dispatch are testable
716	# before any real producer exists. A non-empty string yields exactly one violation;
717	# empty (or omitted) yields none. Runtime call sites in runner.sh pass no argument,
718	# so until D3/D4 land the live path always renders nothing and returns 0.
719	# _runner_template_personas <template> — every persona the template names, one
720	# "<where>|<persona id>" per line: <where> is the section, or section/element
721	# for a map element's own persona (ADR-051 §2).
722	_runner_template_personas() {
723	    awk '
724	        function indent(s,   i) { i = 0; while (substr(s, i+1, 1) == " ") i++; return i }
725	        /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
726	        /^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*:/ { sec = $0; sub(/:.*/, "", sec); el = ""; els_ind = -1; next }
727	        /^[[:space:]]+elements:[[:space:]]*$/ { els_ind = indent($0); next }
728	        els_ind >= 0 && /[^[:space:]]/ && indent($0) <= els_ind { els_ind = -1; el = "" }
729	        els_ind >= 0 && /^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]/ {
730	            el = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]+-[[:space:]]+/, "", el); sub(/^id:[[:space:]]*/, "", el)
731	            sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, "", el); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, "", el); next
732	        }
733	        /^[[:space:]]+persona:[[:space:]]*[^[:space:]#]/ {
734	            id = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]+persona:[[:space:]]*/, "", id); sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, "", id)
735	            gsub(/[[:space:]"\047]/, "", id)
736	            print (el != "" ? sec "/" el : sec) "|" id
737	        }
738	    ' "$1" 2>/dev/null
739	}

745	    case "$mode" in
746	        warn|enforce|off) ;;
747	        *) mode="warn" ;;

751	    [[ "$mode" == "off" ]] && return 0
752

754	    local fail_count=0
755	
756	    # Synthetic violation fixture for unit tests — non-empty arg injects one violation.

758	        violations+=("${_violation_fixture}|SYNTHETIC|fixture|synthetic violation injected by test fixture")

763	    # stage's pin, a map element's, the config default — exists in the target
764	    # repository's .zbuild/plugins/persona or the install. A misspelt persona
765	    # must not quietly run as generic, so this refuses in warn mode too.

774	            violations+=("${_pw}|PERSONA_MISSING|${_pid}|the template names persona '${_pid}', which is in neither the repository's .zbuild/plugins/persona nor the install")

776	        done < <(_runner_template_personas "$_TPL_SOURCE_FILE")

785	    # aggregation loop; the rendered bytes are unchanged.
786	    _inputs_render_violations \
787	        "Startup preflight: persona bindings or required plugins are unresolvable:" \
788	        "Fix: ensure the declared persona id exists under plugins/persona/<id>/manifest.yaml
789	     and that each requires.plugins entry names an installable plugin.
790	     See docs/adr/ADR-051-engine-owned-stage-keyed-data-provision.md." \
791	        "${violations[@]}"

793	    # Emit event (best-effort)
794	    if declare -F eb_emit_event >/dev/null 2>&1; then
795	        eb_emit_event "pipeline.preflight.fail" \
796	            "reason=startup_preflight" \
797	            "violation_count=$fail_count" \
798	            "mode=$mode" 2>/dev/null || true

801	    if [[ "$mode" == "warn" && "$_persona_missing" -eq 0 ]]; then
802	        printf '  ZBUILD_CONTRACT_VALIDATOR=warn — continuing despite startup preflight violations. Set =enforce to fail-fast.\n\n' >&2
803	        return 0
804	    fi

806	    # enforce: fail-closed
807	    return 1
808	}

838	    local start="${_RUNNER_PIPELINE_START_MS:-}"

840	        printf '?s'

863	# pipeline status enum is distinct from plugin verdicts on purpose — this is
864	# a render-only mapping for the terminal banner, NOT an extension of the
865	# verdict table itself.

870	#   failed | interrupted | aborted         → fail  → ✗
871	#   preflight_failed                       → warn  → ⚠
872	#   anything else                          → ⚠ (defensive)

877	        complete_unconverged)          verdict_glyph "warn" ;;
878	        failed|interrupted|aborted)    verdict_glyph "fail" ;;
879	        preflight_failed)              verdict_glyph "warn" ;;
880	        *)                             printf '%s' "?" ;;
881	    esac

898	# ─── _render_pipeline_end <status> [stage] [rc] (#525) ───────────────────────
899	# Emits the terminal banner that closes a pipeline run, framed with ═ (U+2550)
900	# to distinguish the pipeline boundary from the stage divider (━) and stage-io
901	# banners (─). Two-line layout:
902	#
903	#   ════════════════ pipeline.end ════════════════ HH:MM:SS UTC
904	#   <glyph> Pipeline <status_word>: status=<X> run_id=<Y> issue=<N> (took <dur>)
905	#
906	# Frame bars colored BLUE (chrome). Glyph + leading status word inherit the
907	# verdict class color (foreground signal). Right-aligned timestamp via the
908	# same width math as _render_stage_divider — degrades to a symmetric divider
909	# (no timestamp) when mid_bar <= 2.
910	#
911	# Writes to fd 2 so it composes correctly with other operator lines (info /
912	# success / error) under the same output redirection rules. Banner is emitted
913	# AFTER the pipeline.end JSONL event so the durable event is fail-closed
914	# against banner-write failures.
915	_render_pipeline_end() {
916	    local status="${1:-unknown}"
917	    local stage_hint="${2:-}"
918	    local rc_hint="${3:-}"
919	    local run_id="${_runner_run_id:-?}"
920	    local issue="${_runner_issue:-?}"
921	    # Best-effort value gathering. Each `$(...)` here forks a helper that may
922	    # itself fork an external (awk in the duration token, date/tput in the
923	    # clock/width helpers). Most call sites invoke this banner DIRECTLY under the
924	    # runner's `set -e` (e.g. the cycle/stage abort + LLM/scope-abort paths) —
925	    # not wrapped in `|| true` — so a transient under-load fork failure in any
926	    # one of these bare assignments would trip errexit and abort the render
927	    # BEFORE the printf block, silently dropping the operator's terminal banner
928	    # mid-teardown. `|| fallback` neutralizes errexit at each assignment so the
929	    # banner is always emitted once the function is reached, on every call site.
930	    # (#1156)
931	    local dur; dur="$(_runner_pipeline_duration_token)" || dur='?s'
932	    local glyph; glyph="$(_pipeline_status_glyph "$status")" || glyph='✗'
933	    local color; color="$(_pipeline_status_color "$status")" || color=''
934	    local frame="${BLUE:-}"
935	    local ts; ts="$(_runner_now_short)" || ts='??:??:?? UTC'
936	    local width; width="$(_term_width)" || width=80
937	
938	    # Map status → operator-friendly verb for line 2. Tracks event payload
939	    # verbatim so "status=<X>" agrees with the verb. ("success" in legacy
940	    # event payloads renders as "complete" — see ADR-015 §v5 amendment).
941	    local word
942	    case "$status" in
943	        success|complete)        word="complete" ;;
944	        complete_unconverged)    word="complete_unconverged" ;;
945	        failed)                  word="failed" ;;
946	        interrupted)             word="interrupted" ;;
947	        aborted)                 word="aborted" ;;
948	        preflight_failed)        word="preflight_failed" ;;
949	        *)                       word="$status" ;;
950	    esac
951	
952	    local label=" pipeline.end "
953	    # Layout: <left_bar><label><mid_bar> <ts>
954	    local left_bar=$(( (width - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1) / 2 ))
955	    local mid_bar=$(( width - left_bar - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1 ))
956	
957	    local detail_status="status=${status}"
958	    [[ -n "$stage_hint" ]] && detail_status+=" stage=${stage_hint}"
959	    [[ -n "$rc_hint"    ]] && detail_status+=" rc=${rc_hint}"
960	
961	    if [[ "$mid_bar" -le 2 ]]; then
962	        # Degraded layout — drop timestamp from the header.
963	        local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
964	        [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
965	        local bar
966	        printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
967	        bar="${bar// /═}"
968	        {
969	            printf '\n'
970	            printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' "$frame" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" "$frame" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
971	            printf '%b%b%s%b Pipeline %s: %s run_id=%s issue=%s (took %s)\n' \
972	                "$color" "${BOLD:-}" "$glyph" "${RESET:-}" \
973	                "$word" "$detail_status" "$run_id" "$issue" "$dur"
974	        } >&2
975	        _runner_render_open_items "$status" || true
976	        return 0
977	    fi
978	
979	    local lbar rbar
980	    printf -v lbar '%*s' "$left_bar" ''; lbar="${lbar// /═}"
981	    printf -v rbar '%*s' "$mid_bar"  ''; rbar="${rbar// /═}"
982	    {
983	        printf '\n'
984	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b %s\n' \
985	            "$frame" "$lbar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
986	            "$frame" "$rbar" "${RESET:-}" "$ts"
987	        printf '%b%b%s%b Pipeline %s: %s run_id=%s issue=%s (took %s)\n' \
988	            "$color" "${BOLD:-}" "$glyph" "${RESET:-}" \
989	            "$word" "$detail_status" "$run_id" "$issue" "$dur"
990	    } >&2
991	    _runner_render_open_items "$status" || true
992	}
993	
994	# _runner_render_open_items <status> — #2330 (ADR-068 §8): a run that did not
995	# pass ends by saying why in words and naming each open item, with what would
996	# settle it. pipeline.end keeps the engine's code; this is what a reader sees.
997	_runner_render_open_items() {
998	    case "${1:-}" in failed|interrupted|aborted) ;; *) return 0 ;; esac
999	    [[ -n "${_runner_state_file:-}" ]] && declare -F open_items_markdown >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
1000	    local sd="${_runner_state_file%/*}" items n
1001	    items="$(open_items_markdown "$sd")" || items=""
1002	    n=0; [[ -n "$items" ]] && n="$(grep -c '^[0-9][0-9]*\. ' <<< "$items" || true)"
1003	    {
1004	        printf 'The run %s.\n' "$(run_end_words "${_CYCLE_LAST_TERMINATED_REASON:-}" "$n")"
1005	        [[ -n "$items" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$items"
1006	    } >&2
1007	}
1008	
1009	# ─── _render_stage_divider <stage> (#492, ts: #508) ──────────────────────────
1010	# Emits a blank line + a heavy horizontal rule (━ U+2501) with the stage name
1011	# centered in stage-color, then another blank line — written to fd 2 so it
1012	# survives the same redirection rules as ▸/✓/✗ info lines. Used on every
1013	# stage transition (between eb_emit_event "stage.start" and "▸ Running stage")
1014	# so the operator's eye finds the next stage boundary at a glance.
1015	#
1016	# #508: right-align an HH:MM:SS UTC timestamp on the divider, mirroring the
1017	# stage-io banner header right-alignment (_stage_io_compose_banner). Width
1018	# math (no bookend glyphs in this layout — just bars + label + sep + ts):
1019	#   visible = left_bar + len(label) + mid_bar + 1 (space) + len(ts)
1020	#   left_bar = (width - len(label) - len(ts) - 1) / 2
1021	#   mid_bar  = width - left_bar - len(label) - len(ts) - 1
1022	# Degrade rule: when mid_bar <= 2 (very narrow terminals) we drop the
1023	# timestamp and emit the legacy symmetric divider so layout stays legible.
1024	_render_stage_divider() {
1025	    local stage="$1"
1026	    local width
1027	    width="$(_term_width)"
1028	    local color
1029	    color="$(_stage_color "$stage")"
1030	    local label=" ${stage} "
1031	    local ts; ts="$(_runner_now_short)"
1032	
1033	    # Layout: <left_bar><label><mid_bar> <ts>
1034	    # Visible width = left_bar + len(label) + mid_bar + 1 (sep) + len(ts).
1035	    local left_bar=$(( (width - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1) / 2 ))
1036	    local mid_bar=$(( width - left_bar - ${#label} - ${#ts} - 1 ))
1037	
1038	    if [[ "$mid_bar" -le 2 ]]; then
1039	        # Degraded: legacy symmetric divider, no timestamp (narrow terminal).
1040	        local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1041	        [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1042	        local bar
1043	        printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1044	        bar="${bar// /━}"
1045	        {
1046	            printf '\n'
1047	            printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' "$color" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" "$color" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1048	            printf '\n'
1049	            # #523: trailing blank line — combined with the existing leading
1050	            # \n above, produces two stacked blanks between consecutive stages.
1051	            # Cycle sub-dividers (ADR-015 §v6) intentionally do NOT add this.
1052	            printf '\n'
1053	        } >&2
1054	        return 0
1055	    fi
1056	
1057	    local lbar rbar
1058	    printf -v lbar '%*s' "$left_bar" ''; lbar="${lbar// /━}"
1059	    printf -v rbar '%*s' "$mid_bar"  ''; rbar="${rbar// /━}"
1060	    {
1061	        printf '\n'
1062	        # %b on colored fragments so \033[...] resolves like echo -e elsewhere.
1063	        # Timestamp is plain text outside color escapes — NO_COLOR keeps it.
1064	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b %s\n' \
1065	            "$color" "$lbar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1066	            "$color" "$rbar" "${RESET:-}" "$ts"
1067	        printf '\n'
1068	        # #523: trailing blank line — combined with the leading \n above,
1069	        # produces two stacked blanks between consecutive stages. Cycle
1070	        # sub-dividers (ADR-015 §v6) intentionally do NOT add this.
1071	        printf '\n'
1072	    } >&2
1073	}
1074	
1075	# ─── Cycle banner helpers (#524, ADR-015 §v6, ADR-021) ───────────────────────
1076	# Operator-fd-2 chrome for outer cycles (ADR-021). These render a visual
1077	# hierarchy that nests cleanly with the existing stage-transition divider
1078	# (_render_stage_divider) so the operator can see cycle entry, per-iter
1079	# boundaries, per-iter outcomes, and cycle exit in the scrollback.
1080	#
1081	# Glyph + color ladder (heaviest → lightest):
1082	#   ━━━ (U+2501) stage transition   — BOLD BLUE (handled in _render_stage_divider)
1083	#   ═══ (U+2550) cycle entry/exit   — LIGHT_BLUE
1084	#   ─── (U+2500) cycle iter divider — CYAN
1085	#
1086	# Routing contract (silent-failure mitigations):
1087	#   - All 4 helpers write to fd 2 ONLY. Hardcoded `>&2`. NEVER capture in $(…)
1088	#     — output would vanish. Banner emit follows event emit (event=durable,
1089	#     banner=best-effort).
1090	#   - `{ ...; } >&2 2>/dev/null || true` is used so a broken stderr can never
1091	#     abort the cycle. Each block is a single printf wrapped in the redirect
1092	#     group so SIGINT during banner emit cannot race on partial writes.
1093	#   - These banners are fd-2 ONLY and NEVER appear in the PR comment body
1094	#     rendered by gh_comment. Operator chrome only.
1095	#
1096	# Determinism: honors ZBUILD_TERM_WIDTH_OVERRIDE + ZBUILD_STAGE_IO_NOW_MS_OVERRIDE
1097	# via _term_width / _runner_now_short (same contract as _render_stage_divider).
1098	
1099	# ─── _render_cycle_entry <cycle_id> <max> <stages_csv> ───────────────────────
1100	# Heavy `═` LIGHT_BLUE divider + `▸ Entering cycle <id>` line + DIM trailer
1101	# (max + stages). Emitted by the runner BEFORE cycle_orchestrator_run so the
1102	# operator's eye finds the cycle boundary before the first iter divider.
1103	_render_cycle_entry() {
1104	    local cycle_id="$1" max="$2" stages_csv="${3:-}" description="${4:-}"
1105	    local width; width="$(_term_width)"
1106	    local label=" cycle: ${cycle_id} "
1107	    local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1108	    [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1109	    local bar
1110	    printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1111	    bar="${bar// /═}"
1112	    {
1113	        printf '\n'
1114	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' \
1115	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1116	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1117	        printf '%b%b▸%b Entering cycle: %b%b%s%b\n' \
1118	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "${BOLD:-}" "${RESET:-}" \
1119	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "${BOLD:-}" "$cycle_id" "${RESET:-}"
1120	        # #831: operator-facing description on its own DIM line, between the
1121	        # Entering-cycle headline and the (max_iterations=…) trailer. Skipped
1122	        # entirely when description is empty so templates without it render
1123	        # identically to the pre-#831 banner (golden tests stay valid).
1124	        if [[ -n "$description" ]]; then
1125	            printf '%b  %s%b\n' "${DIM:-}" "$description" "${RESET:-}"
1126	        fi
1127	        printf '%b  (max_iterations=%s · stages=%s)%b\n' \
1128	            "${DIM:-}" "$max" "$stages_csv" "${RESET:-}"
1129	        printf '\n'
1130	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1131	}
1132	
1133	# ─── _render_parallel_entry <group_id> <max_parallel> <members_csv> ──────────
1134	# ADR-039 (#1131): clone of _render_cycle_entry for a parallel stage group.
1135	# Heavy `═` LIGHT_BLUE divider + `▸ Entering parallel group <id>` line + DIM
1136	# trailer (max_parallel + members). Emitted by the runner BEFORE
1137	# parallel_group_run so the operator's eye finds the group boundary first.
1138	_render_parallel_entry() {
1139	    local group_id="$1" max="$2" members_csv="${3:-}"
1140	    local width; width="$(_term_width)"
1141	    local label=" parallel: ${group_id} "
1142	    local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1143	    [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1144	    local bar
1145	    printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1146	    bar="${bar// /═}"
1147	    {
1148	        printf '\n'
1149	        printf '%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' \
1150	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1151	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1152	        printf '%b%b▸%b Entering parallel group: %b%b%s%b\n' \
1153	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "${BOLD:-}" "${RESET:-}" \
1154	            "${LIGHT_BLUE:-}" "${BOLD:-}" "$group_id" "${RESET:-}"
1155	        printf '%b  (max_parallel=%s · members=%s)%b\n' \
1156	            "${DIM:-}" "$max" "$members_csv" "${RESET:-}"
1157	        printf '\n'
1158	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1159	}
1160	
1161	# ─── _render_parallel_group_complete <group_id> <member_count> <failure_count> ─
1162	# Issue OUT (ADR-039): DIM trailer after a parallel group's per-member lines,
1163	# mirroring _render_cycle_exit's role for cycles. e.g.
1164	# `▸ review_lenses complete — 5 members, 0 blocking`.
1165	_render_parallel_group_complete() {
1166	    local group_id="$1" count="${2:-0}" fail="${3:-0}"
1167	    {
1168	        printf '%b▸ %s complete — %s members, %s blocking%b\n' \
1169	            "${DIM:-}" "$group_id" "$count" "$fail" "${RESET:-}"
1170	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1171	}
1172	
1173	# ─── _render_cycle_iter_divider <cycle_id> <iter> <max> ───────────────────────
1174	# Light `─` CYAN sub-divider for each iter boundary, e.g.
1175	# `─── build_test_cycle iter 2/5 ─────`. When this cycle is nested inside
1176	# another cycle the orchestrator has already set ZBUILD_SEQ_PREFIX (e.g.
1177	# `4.1`) — surface it as a `[<prefix>]` prefix so operators can tell at a
1178	# glance which outer iter this divider belongs to:
1179	#   outer (no prefix): `─── build_review_cycle iter 1/2 ───`
1180	#   inner (prefix set): `─── [4.1] build_test_cycle iter 1/3 ───`
1181	# Reuses the seq-prefix machinery from Wave 19-B #718 / cycle-orchestrator.sh:888
1182	# — no new plumbing, no hook-signature change. Emitted by the orchestrator's
1183	# iter-begin hook BEFORE the first per-stage banner of the iter.
1184	_render_cycle_iter_divider() {
1185	    local cycle_id="$1" iter="$2" max="$3"
1186	    local prefix="${ZBUILD_SEQ_PREFIX:-}"
1187	    local label
1188	    if [[ -n "$prefix" ]]; then
1189	        label=" [${prefix}] ${cycle_id} iter ${iter}/${max} "
1190	    else
1191	        label=" ${cycle_id} iter ${iter}/${max} "
1192	    fi
1193	    local width; width="$(_term_width)"
1194	    local sides=$(( (width - ${#label}) / 2 ))
1195	    [[ "$sides" -lt 2 ]] && sides=2
1196	    local bar
1197	    printf -v bar '%*s' "$sides" ''
1198	    bar="${bar// /─}"
1199	    {
1200	        printf '\n%b%s%b%s%b%b%s%b\n' \
1201	            "${CYAN:-}" "$bar" "${BOLD:-}" "$label" "${RESET:-}" \
1202	            "${CYAN:-}" "$bar" "${RESET:-}"
1203	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1204	}
1205	
1206	# ─── _render_cycle_iter_complete <iter> <verdict> <score> <fc> <elapsed_s> ──
1207	# Per-iter DIM trailer line e.g. `↳ iter 2 complete: verdict=pass score=-1
1208	# failure_count=1 elapsed=4s`. Emitted by the orchestrator's iter-complete
1209	# hook AFTER the `cycle.iteration.complete` event is durable. #1254: the
1210	# `score` axis (progress − defects) replaced the retired `velocity` label so
1211	# the per-iter line matches the OUTPUT banner's health score.
1212	_render_cycle_iter_complete() {
1213	    local iter="$1" verdict="$2" score="$3" failure_count="$4" elapsed_s="$5"
1214	    {
1215	        printf '%b↳ iter %s complete: verdict=%s score=%s failure_count=%s elapsed=%ss%b\n' \
1216	            "${DIM:-}" "$iter" "$verdict" "$score" "$failure_count" "$elapsed_s" "${RESET:-}"
1217	    } >&2 2>/dev/null || true
1218	}
1219	
1220	# ─── _render_cycle_exit <cycle_id> <reason> <iter> <max> ──────────────────────
1221	# Heavy `═` LIGHT_BLUE divider + verdict-glyph line mapping termination reason
1222	# to glyph + color (see #524 spec).
1223	#   converged       → ✓ GREEN+BOLD
1224	#   max_iterations  → ✗ RED+BOLD
1225	#   plateau         → ✗ RED+BOLD
1226	#   divergence      → ✗ RED+BOLD
1227	#   aborted         → ⚠ YELLOW+BOLD
